zh: “话虽如此，我未免受之有愧。”
en: “Even so, I cannot help feeling that I do not deserve it.”

zh: “这不须如此想。倒是那位在你穷途之际，慷慨援手的胡君，别人非亲非故帮你的忙，无非看你是个人才，会有一番事业，你该记着这一点！”
en: “You needn't think that way. But you must remember Mr Hu, who generously helped you when you had nowhere to turn. He was neither a relative nor an old family friend. He helped because he saw ability in you and believed you could accomplish something. You should keep that in mind.”

zh: 王有龄自然深深受教。他本来就不是没有大志，连番奇遇的鼓舞，越发激起一片雄心，只一闭上眼，便看得前程锦绣，目迷神眩，虽还未补缺，却已在享受做官的乐趣了。
en: Wang took the advice deeply to heart. He had never lacked ambition, and these successive strokes of fortune stirred it still further. Whenever he closed his eyes, he saw a future of dazzling promise. Though he had not yet obtained an appointment, he was already savouring the pleasures of office.

zh: 第二天早晨起身，何桂清已写好了一封致黄宗汉的信在等他。这封信不是泛泛的八行，甚至也不象一封荐信，里面谈了许多知交的私话，然后才提到王有龄，说是“总角之交，谊如昆季”，特为嘱他指捐分发浙江，以便请黄宗汉培植造就，照这封信的恳切结实来说，就差何桂清当面拱手拜托了。
en: When he rose the next morning, He Guiqing was waiting with a letter to Huang Zonghan. It was no ordinary note of introduction; indeed, it scarcely resembled a recommendation at all. Much of it concerned private matters between close friends. Only then did it mention Wang, describing him as “a friend since boyhood, as dear as a brother,” whom He had specifically advised to purchase assignment to Zhejiang so that Huang might nurture his abilities and advance his career. The letter was so earnest and substantial that little was lacking except He's presence in person, hands clasped in appeal.

zh: 等看过封好，王有龄便跟何桂清要人。以他的意思，很想请杨承福做个帮手，这一点何桂清无法满足他的希望，因为杨承福是他最得力的人，许多公事、关系只有他清楚首尾，非他人所能替代。
en: After Wang had read it and it had been sealed, he asked He to provide someone to accompany him. He very much wanted Yang Chengfu, but this was a wish his friend could not grant. Yang was his most capable assistant. Many official matters and personal connections were fully understood by Yang alone; no one could replace him.

zh: “这样吧，”杨承福建议，“叫高升跟了王老爷去，也很妥当。”
en: “Why not send Gao Sheng with His Honour?” Yang suggested. “That would work very well.”

zh: 高升也很诚实能干，他自己也愿意跟王有龄，事情就算定局。拜别何桂清，谢了杨承福，由高升照料着，当天就到了京里。本来想住会馆，因为本年王子恩科，明年癸丑正科，接连两年会试，落第的、新到的举人，挤得满坑满谷，要找一间空房实在很难。而且三有龄以监生的底子来加捐，跟那些明年四月便可一举成名的举人在一起，相形之下，仙凡异途，也自觉难堪。
en: Gao Sheng was honest and capable too, and willing to accompany Wang, so the arrangement was settled. Wang took leave of He Guiqing, thanked Yang, and, under Gao's care, reached the capital that same day. He had intended to stay at the provincial guildhall. But the current renzi year had brought a special examination, and the following guichou year would bring the regular one. With metropolitan examinations in two successive years, unsuccessful candidates and newly arrived provincial graduates packed the place. An empty room was almost impossible to find. Moreover, Wang was seeking to upgrade a purchased qualification on the basis of his Imperial Academy status. Beside provincial graduates who might win distinction in the fourth month, he felt that he belonged to a lesser world, and the comparison embarrassed him.

zh: 便索性破费些，在两河沿找了家客店住。
en: He therefore decided to spend a little more and take a room at an inn in Liangheyan.

zh: 天气极冷，生了炉子还象坐在冰害里，高开上街买了皮纸和面，在炉子上打了一盆浆糊。把皮纸裁成两指宽的纸条，把窗户板壁上所有的缝隙都糊没。西北风进不来，炉人才能发生作用，立刻满室生春，十分舒服。王有龄吃过晚饭，便跟高开商量正事。
en: The weather was bitterly cold. Even with a stove burning, the room felt like an ice cellar. Gao went out to buy tough paper and flour, then cooked a basin of paste on the stove. Cutting the paper into strips two fingers wide, he sealed every crack in the windows and wooden partitions. Once the northwest wind was shut out, the stove could do its work. The room soon felt as warm as spring. After supper, Wang discussed their business with him.

zh: “老爷，我有个主意，你看使得使不得？”离升说道，“明天就是腊八，还有十几天工夫就‘封印’了。”
en: “Your Honour, I have an idea. See what you think of it,” Gao said. “Tomorrow is the eighth day of the last month. In little more than ten days, the government offices will seal up their official seals for the New Year.”

zh: “啊！”一下提醒了王有龄，“一‘封印’就是一个月，这十几天办不成，在京里过年空等，那耽误的工夫就大了。”
en: “Ah!” Wang suddenly remembered. “Once the seals are put away, the offices will be closed for a month. If we cannot finish in these ten-odd days, we'll have to spend the New Year here waiting. That would mean a long delay.”

zh: “最啊！打哪儿来说，都是件划不来的事。所以我在想，不如多花几个钱，尽这十几天把事情办妥，赶年里就动身回南。”
en: “Exactly. Whichever way you look at it, that would be a poor bargain. I was thinking that it might be better to spend a little extra and finish the business before the offices close, then set off south before the year ends.”

zh: “年里就动身？不太急了吗？”
en: “Before the year ends? Wouldn't that be rather hurried?”

zh: “我是替老爷打算。京里如果没有什么熟人，在店里过年，也不是味儿。再说从大年初一到元宵，到哪儿也得大把花钱，真正划不来。与其这个样，莫如就在路上过年。再有一层，“高升凑近了他说，”老爷最好赶在何大人之前，或者差不多的日子到浙江见黄抚合，何大人的信才管用。“
en: “I'm thinking of your interests, sir. If you have few friends in the capital, spending the New Year at an inn won't be much pleasure. Besides, from New Year's Day to the Lantern Festival, you have to spend freely wherever you go. It really isn't worth it. Better to spend the holiday on the road. There's another point.” Gao leaned closer. “It would be best to reach Zhejiang and see Governor Huang before His Excellency He arrives, or at about the same time. That's when his letter will carry weight.”

zh: 王有龄恍然大悟，觉得高升的话，实在有见识。黄宗汉此人既有刻薄的名声，保不定在椿寿那件案子结束以后，过河拆桥，不买何桂清的帐。如果正是何桂清到浙江查案时，有求于人，情形自然不同。总之，宁早勿迟，无论如何不错。
en: Wang understood at once and recognised the wisdom of Gao's advice. Huang had a reputation for harshness. Once Chunshou's case was settled, he might well discard the man who had helped him and cease to oblige He Guiqing. While He was in Zhejiang investigating the case, Huang would still need his goodwill, and the situation would be different. In any event, arriving sooner rather than later could only be the right course.

zh: “我听你的话，就这么办。不过，你可有路子呢？”
en: “I'll take your advice. Let's do that. But do you know how to go about it?”

zh: “路子总有的。明天我就去找。”高升极有把握地说：“包管又便宜又好。”
en: “There will be a way. I'll start looking tomorrow,” Gao answered confidently. “I'll see that it is done well and at a reasonable cost.”

zh: 于是王有龄欣然开了箱子，把旧捐的盐大使“部照”取了出来，接着磨墨伸纸开具“三代”，细陈经历，把文件都预备妥当，一一交代明白。又取二十两银子交给高升，作为应酬花费。
en: Pleased, Wang opened his trunk and took out the Board's certificate for his original purchased qualification as a salt-station superintendent. He then ground ink, spread out paper, and prepared a statement of his ancestry for three generations and a detailed account of his background. Once the documents were ready, he explained everything to Gao and gave him twenty taels for the expenses of making the necessary contacts.

zh: 从第二天起，高升开始奔走。起初的消息不大好，不是说时间上没有把握，就是额外需索的费用太高。这样过了三四天，不但王有龄心里焦灼，连高升自己也有些气馁了。
en: Gao began his rounds the next day. The first reports were discouraging: either completion in time could not be guaranteed, or the extra fees demanded were too high. Three or four days passed. Wang grew anxious, and even Gao began to lose heart.

zh: 就在放弃希望，打算着在京过年时，事情突然有了转机，吏部有个书办，家里遭了回禄之灾，还烧死了一母一子，年近岁逼，逢此家破人亡的惨事，偏偏这书办又因案下狱，雪上加霜，濒临绝境，必须求援于他的同事们。
en: Just as they were abandoning hope and preparing to spend the New Year in the capital, matters unexpectedly changed. A clerk at the Board of Civil Appointments had suffered a fire at home in which a mother and child had died. With the year drawing to a close, his household was ruined. To make matters worse, he himself was in prison over a case. Desperate and with nowhere else to turn, he had to appeal to his colleagues.

zh: 帮忙无非“有饯出钱，有力出力”，但出钱的不过十两、八两银子，倒是出力的帮忙得大。年下公事特忙，部里从司官到书办，知道各省差官，以及本人来候选捐纳，谋干前程的，都希望提前办理，在京里过年，赔贴盘缠，空耗辰光还不说，有些限期的公事，耽误了还有处分。所以这时是留难需索，择肥而噬的好机会，现在为了帮同事的忙，他们私下定了章程，出了“公价”，凡是想限期办妥的公事，除了照平时的行市纳规费以外，另外看情况加送若干，多下的钱就归那遭祸的书办所得。对外人来说，这比自己去撞木钟，辗转托人，重重剥削要便宜得多。
en: Helping meant contributing money if one had it, or effort if one could. Financial contributions amounted to no more than eight or ten taels apiece; practical assistance proved more substantial. Official business was especially heavy before the New Year. From departmental officials down to clerks, everyone knew that provincial messengers and men seeking appointments or purchasing qualifications wanted their affairs settled early. Spending the holiday in the capital meant wasted time and additional living costs; missing a deadline on official business might also bring punishment. It was therefore an ideal opportunity to obstruct proceedings and extract money from those who could pay. To assist their unfortunate colleague, the clerks privately agreed on a standard schedule of charges. Anyone wanting business completed within a fixed time would pay the usual unofficial fees, plus an extra sum according to the circumstances. The addition would go to the stricken clerk. For outsiders, this was much cheaper than trying their luck, seeking one intermediary after another, and being fleeced at every stage.

zh: 高升从琉璃厂的笔墨庄里得到了这个消息，又去找熟人打听，果有其事，匆忙回来说与王有龄。就托那个熟人，代为接洽，说定了价钱，一共四百八十两银子，加捐为候补州县，分发浙江。其中三分之二“正项”，三分之一是“杂费”，打成两张银票，正项自己去缴，杂费托经手人转交，不过五天工夫，就把簇新的一张“部照”和称为“实收”的捐纳交银收据都拿到手了。
en: Gao heard of the arrangement at a brush-and-ink shop in Liulichang. He checked with an acquaintance, confirmed that it was real, and hurried back to tell Wang. Through this acquaintance they negotiated a total of 480 taels to upgrade Wang's qualification to an expectant local magistracy with assignment to Zhejiang. Two-thirds represented the official payment; one-third covered miscellaneous expenses. They obtained two bank drafts. Wang paid the official amount himself, while the intermediary delivered the other. In only five days, Wang had both a new certificate from the Board and the official receipt for his contribution.

zh: 这件大事倒办好了，长行回南，却颇费周章。急景调年，车船都不大愿意做此一笔买卖。王有龄便又跟高升商议，大事已妥，随时可走，也不争在这几天，不如过了“破五”再说。高升原是为主人打算，唯命是从，当时使先订好了两辆大车，付了一半车价，约定开年初七、宜于长行的黄道吉日动身。
en: The main business was settled, but arranging the long journey south proved troublesome. With the year almost over, carters and boatmen were reluctant to undertake it. Wang consulted Gao again. Now that everything important was done, they could leave whenever they wished; a few days made little difference. Why not wait until after the fifth day of the New Year? Gao's only concern was his master's interests, and he accepted the decision. They booked two large carts, paid half the fare, and agreed to depart on the seventh day, an auspicious date for a long journey.

zh: 这时京里除了军机处，大小衙门，都已封印。满街都是匆匆忙忙的行人，有的忧容满面，四处告帮过年，有的提着灯笼，星夜讨债。王有龄却是心定神闲，每天由高升领着，到各处去闲逛。他在京里也有些熟人，但一则年节下大家都忙，不便去打搅，二则带的土仪不多，空手登门拜访，于礼不台，三则是他自己觉得现在境况不佳，不如下见，等将来得意了，欢然道故，才有人情酬醉之乐。因此，除了极少的一两家至亲，登门一揖以外，其余同乡亲友那里，一概下去。
en: By then, every government office except the Grand Council had closed for the holiday. The streets were full of hurried figures: some wore anxious faces as they sought help to get through the New Year; others carried lanterns and pursued debts late into the night. Wang, however, was at ease and went sightseeing with Gao every day. He knew some people in the capital, but there were several reasons not to visit. Everyone was busy with the holiday, and he did not wish to disturb them. He had few local gifts left, and arriving empty-handed would be discourteous. He also felt that his present circumstances were not impressive enough. Better to wait until he had prospered; then recalling old times would bring the real pleasure of friendly hospitality. Apart from brief calls on one or two close relatives, he visited none of his fellow provincials or other friends.

zh: 到了大年三十，会馆里的执事邀去过年，吃完年夜饭，厅上拉开桌子，摇摊的摇摊，推牌九的推牌九，王有龄不好此道，早早回到了西河沿客店。
en: On New Year's Eve, the guildhall stewards invited him to join their celebration. After dinner, tables were set up in the hall for various forms of gambling, including the shaking of counters and games of pai gow. Wang had no taste for these pursuits and returned early to his inn at Xiheyan.

zh: 高升是他事先放了他假的，不在客店。伙计替他拨旺了炉人，沏了热茶，枯坐无聊，又弄了酒来喝，无奈“独醉不成欢”，有心摘一朵野花，点缀佳节，想想自己已是“父母官”的身分，怕让高升发觉了瞧不起。“八大胡同”倒是近在咫尺，但“清吟小班”是有名的销金窝，这一年异遇甚多，保不定又逢一段奇缘，那一下，五百年前的风流债还不情，岂不辜负了胡、何二人的盛情厚望？
en: He had already given Gao the evening off, so the servant was away. An inn attendant stirred up the stove and made fresh tea. Bored with sitting alone, Wang ordered some wine, but drinking by himself brought no cheer. He considered seeking a woman's company to enliven the festival, then remembered that he was now qualified to become a magistrate, a parent to the people. He feared Gao would find out and think less of him. The Eight Great Lanes were close by, but their fashionable singing houses were notorious places to squander money. After so many strange encounters that year, who knew whether another romance might await him? If he became entangled in some endless debt of passion, would he not betray the generosity and hopes of both Hu and He?

zh: 在满街爆竹声中，王有龄一个人悄俏地睡下了，却是怎么样也没有睡意。
en: Amid firecrackers sounding throughout the streets, Wang quietly went to bed alone. Yet sleep would not come.

zh: 通前彻后，细思平生，有凄凉，也有欢欣，有感慨，却更多希望。他在想，不走何桂清那样的“正途”，已是输人一着，但也不能就此认输，一个人总要能展其所长，虽说书读得没有何桂清好，但从小跟在父亲身边，了解民生，熟悉吏治，以及吃苦耐劳，习于交接，却不是那班埋首窗下，不通世务的书生可比。“世事洞明皆学问”，妄自匪薄，志气消沉，聪明才智也就灰塞萎缩了。于今逢到大好机会，又正当国家多事，明主求治之际，风尘俗吏的作为，亦未见得会比金马玉堂的学士逊色！
en: Looking back over his life, he found sadness and joy, much to reflect on, and still more to hope for. By failing to take the regular examination route as He Guiqing had done, he had already fallen behind. But that was no reason to admit defeat. A man must develop his own strengths. He might be less learned than He, yet he had grown up beside his father, observing people's livelihoods, becoming familiar with administration, learning to endure hardship, and dealing with all sorts of people. In these things, scholars buried in their books and ignorant of the world could not compare with him. “A thorough understanding of human affairs is itself learning.” If he belittled himself and lost his ambition, his abilities would only wither. Now a splendid opportunity had come, at a time when the country faced grave difficulties and an enlightened ruler sought effective government. A practical official seasoned by the world might achieve as much as a scholar in the splendid halls of court.

zh: 转念到此，顿时浮起一片要做一番事业的雄心壮志。但以大器自期，觉得肚子里的货色还不够，不是同赋文章，而是于国计民生有关的学问。
en: These reflections stirred a powerful determination to accomplish something. Yet if he expected great things of himself, he needed more knowledge—not poetry and elegant essays, but learning relevant to the country's administration and the people's welfare.

zh: 因此年初一那天逛琉璃厂，别人买吃的、玩的，王有时象那些好书成癖的名士一样，只在书铺里坐。王有龄此时的气度服饰，已非昔比，掌柜的十分巴结，先拜了年，摆上果盘，然后请教姓氏、乡里、科名。
en: Thus, when he visited Liulichang on New Year's Day, while others bought food and amusements, Wang remained in the bookshops like a scholar with a passion for collecting books. His bearing and clothes were now very different from before. The proprietor was eager to please him: first New Year greetings, then a plate of fruit, and finally polite inquiries about his surname, home province, and examination achievements.

zh: “敝姓王，福建，秋闹刚刚侥幸。”王有龄的口气是自表新科举人，好在“王”是大姓，便冒充了也不怕拆穿。
en: “My surname is Wang. I'm from Fujian. I was fortunate enough to pass last autumn.” He spoke as though he were a newly qualified provincial graduate. Wang was such a common surname that he felt safe from exposure.

zh: “喔，喔”王老爷春风满面，本科一定‘联捷’。预贺，预贺！“
en: “Ah, indeed! With good fortune shining in your face, Your Honour is certain to succeed again in the coming metropolitan examination. My congratulations in advance!”

zh: “ 谢谢。‘场中莫论文’，看运气罢了。”
en: “Thank you. In the examination hall, literary merit is no guarantee. We must leave it to luck.”

zh: “王老爷说得好一口官话，想来随老太爷在外多年？”
en: “Your Honour speaks excellent Mandarin. You must have spent many years accompanying your father away from home.”

zh: “是的。”王有龄心想，再盘问下去要露马脚了，便即问道：“可有什么实用之学的好书？”
en: “Yes.” Further questions might expose him, Wang thought. He promptly changed the subject. “Have you any good books on practical affairs?”

zh: “怎么没有？”那掌柜想了想，自己从书架子取了部新书来，“这部书，不知王老爷有没有？”
en: “Certainly.” The proprietor considered, then took a new set of books from a shelf himself. “Does Your Honour already own this?”

zh: 一看是贺长龄的《皇朝经世文编》王有龄久闻其名，欣然答道：“我要一部。”
en: It was He Changling's Collected Essays on Statecraft under the Present Dynasty. Wang had long heard of it and replied with pleasure, “I'll take a set.”

zh: “这部书实在好。当今讲究实学，读熟了这部书，殿试策论一定出色。”
en: “An excellent work. Practical learning is much valued nowadays. Master this book, and your policy essay in the palace examination is bound to be distinguished.”

zh: “有没有‘洋务’上的书？”
en: “Have you any books on foreign affairs?”

zh: “讲洋务，有部贵省林大人编的书，非看不可。”
en: “On that subject, there is a work compiled by His Excellency Lin of your own province that you must read.”

zh: 那是林则徐编的《四洲志》，王有龄也买了。书店掌柜看出王有龄所要的是些什么书，牵连不断，搬出一大堆来，一时也无暇细看内容，好在价钱多还公道，便来者不拒，捆载而旧。
en: This was Lin Zexu's Account of the Four Continents, which Wang also bought. Understanding now what his customer wanted, the proprietor brought out one related work after another until a pile had accumulated. There was no time to inspect them all closely, but the prices were generally fair, so Wang accepted them and had them bundled up to take back.

zh: 从这天起，王有龄就在客店里“闭户读书”，把一部《皇朝经世文编》中，谈盐法、河务、漕运的文章，反复研读，一个字都不肯轻易放过。他对湖南安化陶文毅公陶澍的政绩，原就敬仰已久，此时看了那些奏议、条陈，了解了改革盐法槽运的经过，越发向往。同时也有了一个心得，兴利不难，难于除弊！“革路蓝缕，以启山林”，只要功夫用到了，自能生利，但已生之种，为人侵渔把持，弊端丛生，要去消除，使成了侵害人的“权利”，自会遭遇到极大的反抗阻挠。他看陶澍的整顿盐务，改革漕运，论办法也不过实事求是，期于允当，并没有什么了不得的地方，所可贵的是，他的除弊的决心与魄力。
en: From that day onward, he shut himself in his room to study. He repeatedly read the essays on salt administration, river management, and grain transport in the Collected Essays on Statecraft, unwilling to pass lightly over a single word. He had long admired the achievements of Tao Shu of Anhua, Hunan, posthumously honoured as Wenyi. Reading these memorials and proposals, and learning how the reforms of salt administration and grain transport had been carried out, deepened his admiration. He also reached a conclusion of his own: creating benefits was not the hardest task; removing abuses was. To open up new ground through hardship, effort was enough to produce results. Once those benefits existed, however, people appropriated and controlled them until abuses multiplied. Removing the abuses then meant infringing what those people regarded as their rights, and fierce resistance was inevitable. Tao's methods themselves were not extraordinary. He had sought truth in the facts and aimed at workable, fair arrangements. What deserved admiration was his determination and courage in abolishing abuses.

zh: 这又归结到一个要点：权力。王有龄在想：俗语说的“大丈夫不可一日无权”，话实在不错。不过这个道理要从反面来看。有权在手，不能有所作为，庸庸碌碌，随波逐流，则虽未作恶，其恶与小人相等，因为官场弊端，就是在此辈手中变得根深蒂固，积重难返的。
en: This led to a further essential point: power. The saying that a capable man cannot go a day without authority was true, Wang thought, but its meaning had to be considered from the other side. A man who held power yet accomplished nothing, drifting along in mediocrity, might commit no direct wrongdoing. Still, his harm was no less than that of a villain, for it was through men like him that official abuses became deeply rooted and almost impossible to remove.

zh: 由于有用世之志，不得不留意时局，正好客店里到了一个湖北来的差官，就住在他间壁，客中寂寞，携酒消夜，谈起两湖的情形，王有龄才知道洪杨军攻长沙不下，克宁乡、益阳，拥有了几千艘发船，出临资口，渡侗庭湖，占领岳州，乘胜东下，十一月陷汉阳，十二月里省城武昌也失守了！巡抚常大淳、学政、藩司、臬司、提督、总兵，还有道员、知府、知县、同知，几乎全城文武，无不身亡。说到悲惨之外，那差官把眼泪掉落在酒杯里。
en: His wish to serve the country compelled him to follow current events. By chance, an official messenger from Hubei arrived at the inn and occupied the next room. Lonely away from home, they shared wine one evening and discussed Hunan and Hubei. Wang learned that, after failing to take Changsha, the forces of Hong and Yang had captured Ningxiang and Yiyang, acquired several thousand boats, emerged at Linzikou, crossed Lake Dongting, and occupied Yuezhou. Pressing eastward, they had taken Hanyang in the eleventh month and the provincial capital, Wuchang, in the twelfth. Governor Chang Dachun, the education commissioner, the provincial treasurer, the judicial commissioner, the provincial military commander, the brigade commanders, and the circuit intendants, prefects, magistrates, and deputy prefects—almost all the city's civil and military officials had died. At the most tragic passages of his account, the messenger's tears fell into his wine cup.

zh: 王有龄也为之惨然停杯。常大淳由浙江巡抚调湖北，还不到一年，他在杭州曾经见过，纯粹是个秉性仁柔的书生，只因为在浙江巡抚往内平治过海盗，朝廷当他会用兵，调到湖北去阻遏洪杨军，结果与城同亡，说起来死得有点冤枉。
en: Wang too set down his cup in sorrow. Less than a year had passed since Chang Dachun's transfer from Zhejiang to Hubei. Wang had seen him in Hangzhou: a scholar of gentle and kindly temperament. Because he had suppressed pirates while governing Zhejiang, the court had assumed that he understood warfare and sent him to Hubei to halt Hong and Yang's advance. He had died with the city. In a sense, his death was a grievous injustice.

zh: 但是，地方官守上有责，而且朝廷已有旨意，派在籍大臣办理“团练”，以求自保，生逢乱世，哪里管得到文是文，武是武？必须得有“上马杀贼，下马草露布”的本理，做官才能出人头地。有了这层省悟，玉有龄又到琉璃厂去买了些《圣武记》之类谈征点方略、练兵筹饷的书，预备利用旅途，好好看他一遍。
en: Yet local officials were responsible for defending their territories. The court had already ordered senior officials living in retirement to organise local militias for self-defence. In a troubled age, who could insist that civil and military duties remain separate? To distinguish himself in office, a man needed the ability to mount a horse and fight, then dismount and write the announcement of victory. Recognising this, Wang returned to Liulichang and bought works such as Records of Imperial Military Achievements, dealing with campaign strategy, troop training, and military finance. He intended to read them carefully on his journey.

zh: 依照约定的日子，正月初七一早，由陆路自京师动身，经长辛店一直南下，出京除了由天津走海道以外，水陆两途在山东边境的德州文汇，运河自京东来，过此偏向西南，经临清、东昌南下，陆路自京西来，过此偏向东南，由平原、禹城、泰安、临沂，进入江苏省境，到清江浦，水陆两途又文汇了。
en: On the appointed day, the seventh of the first month, he left the capital early by road, heading south through Changxindian. Apart from the sea route through Tianjin, the land and water routes out of the capital met at Dezhou on the Shandong border. The canal approached from the east of the capital, then turned southwest through Linqing and Dongchang. The road came from the west and turned southeast through Pingyuan, Yucheng, Tai'an, and Linyi into Jiangsu. At Qingjiangpu, the two routes met again.

zh: 王有龄陆路走了二十天，在整天颠簸的大车中，依旧于不释卷，到晚宿店，豆大油灯下还做笔记。就这样把《经世文编》、《圣武记》、《四洲志》都已看完。有时车中默想，自觉内而漕、盐、兵事，外面夷情洋务，大致都已了然于胸。
en: For twenty days on the road, Wang kept a book in his hands despite the cart's constant jolting. At night, in the inns, he continued taking notes beneath the tiny flame of an oil lamp. In this way he finished the Collected Essays on Statecraft, Records of Imperial Military Achievements, and Account of the Four Continents. Sometimes, reflecting in the cart, he felt that he now had a general grasp of grain transport, salt administration, and military affairs at home, as well as conditions abroad and relations with foreign countries.

zh: 他在路上早就打算好了。车子讲定到王家营子，渡过黄河就是清江浦，由此再雇船沿运河直放杭州。为了印证所学，不妨趁此弃车换船的机会，在情江浦好好住几天。这个以韩信而名闻天下的古淮阴，是南来水陆要冲的第一大码头，江南河道总督专驻此地，河务、漕运、以及淮盐的运销，都以此此为枢纽，能够实地考察一番，真个“胜读十年书”。
en: He had already planned the next stage of his journey. The carts were hired as far as Wangjiayingzi. Across the Yellow River lay Qingjiangpu, where he would hire a boat to take him along the canal to Hangzhou. To test his reading against reality, he might spend a few days there while changing from cart to boat. This was ancient Huaiyin, famous as the home of Han Xin, and the foremost junction of land and water routes for travellers coming from the south. The governor-general of the southern river administration was stationed there. River management, grain transport, and the distribution of Huai salt all centred upon the town. A firsthand investigation would truly be worth ten years of reading.

zh: 哪知来到王家营子，就听说太平军起兵，越发厉害。一到清江浦，立刻就能闻到一种风声鹤嗅的味道，车马络绎，负载着乱糟糟的家具杂物，衣冠不整，口音杂出的异乡人，不计其数，个个脸上有惊惶忧郁的神色，显而易见的，都是些从南而逃来的难民。
en: But at Wangjiayingzi he heard that the Taiping advance was growing ever more alarming. Upon reaching Qingjiangpu, he immediately sensed panic in the air. An endless stream of carts and horses carried disorderly loads of furniture and household goods. Countless strangers in dishevelled clothes spoke in unfamiliar accents, every face anxious and distressed. Plainly, they were refugees fleeing from the south.

zh: “老爷！”高升悄悄说道，“大事不妙！我看客店怕都客满了。带着行李去瞎闯，累赘得很。他老先在茶馆坐一坐，看好了行李，我找店，找妥当了再来请者爷过去。”
en: “Your Honour,” Gao said quietly, “things look bad. I fear the inns will all be full. Dragging the luggage from one to another would be a burden. Why don't you sit in a teahouse and watch it while I find us a room? Once I've secured one, I'll come back for you.”

zh: “好，好！”王有龄抬头一望，路南就是一家大茶馆，便说，“我就在这里等。”
en: “Very well.” Looking up, Wang saw a large teahouse on the south side of the street. “I'll wait here.”

zh: 到了茶馆，先把行李堆在一边，开发了挑侍，要找座头休息。举目四顾，乱哄哄一片，只有当门之处一张直摆的长桌子空着。高升便走过去拂拂凳子上的尘土说道：“老爷请这里坐！”
en: Inside, they stacked their luggage to one side and paid the porter, then looked for somewhere to sit. The place was noisy and crowded. Only a long table set lengthwise by the entrance was empty. Gao went over, dusted a bench, and said, “Please sit here, sir.”

zh: 他是北方人，没有在南方水路上走过，不懂其中的规矩。王有龄却略微有些知道，那张桌子叫“马头桌子”，要漕帮里的“尤头”才有资格坐，所以慌忙拉住高升：“这里坐不得！”
en: He was a northerner who had never travelled the southern waterways and knew nothing of their customs. Wang knew a little. That was the “head table,” reserved for leaders of the grain-transport fraternity. He hastily caught Gao's arm. “You can't sit there!”

zh: “噢！”高升一愣。
en: “Oh!” Gao stopped in surprise.

zh: 王有龄此时无法跟他细说，同时茶博士也已赶了来招呼他与人拼桌。高升见安顿好了，也就匆匆自去。王有龄喝着茶，便向同桌的人打听消息。
en: There was no time for an explanation, and a tea attendant had already come to find Wang a place at another table. Once his master was settled, Gao hurried off. Over his tea, Wang asked his companions for news.

zh: 消息坏得很？自武昌失守，洪杨军有了大小船只一万多艘。把金银财货，军械粮食，都装了上去，又用了几十万老百姓，沿着长江两岸，长驱而东。
en: The news was dreadful. Since the fall of Wuchang, Hong and Yang's army had acquired more than ten thousand vessels of all sizes. They loaded them with gold, silver, other valuables, weapons, and provisions, and drove eastward along both banks of the Yangtze with hundreds of thousands of civilians.

zh: 就这样一直到了广济县的武穴镇，跟两江总督陆建瀛碰上了。
en: At Wuxue, a town in Guangji county, they encountered Lu Jianying, governor-general of Liangjiang.

zh: 湖北不归两江总督所管，陆建瀛是以钦差大臣的身分，出省迎敌。绿营暮气沉沉，早已不能打仗，新招募的兵又没有多少，哪经得住洪杨军如山洪暴发般顺流直冲，以致节节败退。
en: Hubei lay outside his jurisdiction. He had entered the province as an imperial commissioner to meet the enemy. The Green Standard troops were exhausted in spirit and had long since lost their ability to fight, while the newly recruited forces were few. They could not withstand Hong and Yang's men pouring downstream like a mountain torrent and fell back at every engagement.

zh: 这时洪杨军的水师，也由九江，过湖口、彭泽，到了安微省境。守小孤山的江苏按察使，弃防而逃，这一下省城安庆的门户洞开。安徽巡抚蒋文庆只有两干多兵守城，陆建瀛兵败过境，不肯留守，直回江宁。蒋文庆看看保不住，把库款、粮食、军人的一部分，侈运庐州，自己坚守危城。其时城里守卒已经溃散，洪杨军轻而易举地破了城，蒋文庆被杀于抚署西辕门。这是十天前的事。
en: Meanwhile, the rebels' fleet passed Jiujiang, Hukou, and Pengze and entered Anhui. The judicial commissioner of Jiangsu, defending Xiaogushan, abandoned his position and fled, leaving the approach to Anqing, the provincial capital, wide open. Governor Jiang Wenqing had only a little over two thousand men to defend the city. Lu Jianying passed through after his defeat but refused to remain and went straight back to Jiangning. Seeing little hope of holding out, Jiang transferred part of the treasury funds, provisions, and weapons to Luzhou, then stayed to defend the endangered city. By then the garrison had already dispersed. Hong and Yang's men took the city easily, and Jiang was killed at the western outer gate of the governor's compound. This had happened ten days earlier.

zh: “十天前？”王有龄大惊问道：“那么现在‘长毛’到了什么地方了呢？”
en: “Ten days ago?” Wang exclaimed in alarm. “Where are the Long-Haired rebels now, then?”

zh: “这可就不知道了。”那茶客摇摇头，愁容满面的，“芜湖大概总到了。说不定已到了江宁。“
en: “That I don't know.” His fellow customer shook his head, looking deeply troubled. “They must have reached Wuhu. Perhaps they're at Jiangning already.”

zh: 王有龄大惊失色！洪杨军用兵能如此神速？他有点将信将疑。但稍为定一定心来想，亦无足奇，这就是他在旅途中读了许多书的好处，自古以来，长江以上游荆州为重镇，上游一失，顺流东下，下游一定不保，所以历史上南朝如定都金陵，必遣大将镇荆襄，保上游，而荆襄有变，金陵就如俎上之肉，此所以桓温在荆州，东晋君臣，寝食难安，而南唐李氏以上游早失，终于为宋太祖所平。
en: Wang turned pale. Could the army have moved so fast? He found it difficult to believe. But when he steadied himself and thought, it was not surprising. Here his reading on the journey served him well. Since ancient times, Jingzhou had been the strategic stronghold of the upper Yangtze. Once the upper reaches were lost, an enemy could sweep downstream, and the lower reaches could scarcely be held. Thus, southern dynasties that made Jinling their capital always stationed able commanders in Jingzhou and Xiangyang to protect the upper river. If that region changed hands, Jinling was like meat on a chopping board. Hence the sleepless anxiety of the Eastern Jin court while Huan Wen controlled Jingzhou, and the eventual conquest of the Southern Tang by the founding Song emperor after its upper-river defences had been lost.

zh: 这一下，他对当前的形势得失，立刻便有了一个看法，朝中根本无知将略的人，置重兵于湖广、河南、防洪杨北上，却忽略了江南的空虚，这是把他们逼向东南财赋之区，实在是极大的失策。
en: He immediately formed a judgement of the present situation. No one at court seemed to understand strategy. They had concentrated troops in Hunan, Hubei, and Henan to prevent the rebels from moving north, while overlooking the weakness of the lower Yangtze region. This had driven the enemy towards the southeast, the country's great source of revenue. It was a grave mistake.

zh: 照这情形看，金陵迟早不保。他想到何桂清，一颗心猛然往下一沉，随即记起，问桂清不在金陵，抹一抹额上的汗，松口气失声自语：“还好，还好！”
en: Jinling, it seemed, must fall sooner or later. Thinking of He Guiqing, Wang's heart suddenly sank. Then he remembered that He was not in Jinling. Wiping the sweat from his forehead, he breathed out and murmured, “Thank goodness! Thank goodness!”

zh: 同桌的茶客抬起忧郁的双眼望着他，他才发觉自己的失态，便陪着笑说，“我想起一个好朋友，他……”王有龄忽然问道：“请问，学台衙门，可是在江阴？”
en: His companions looked up at him with troubled eyes. Realising that he had behaved oddly, he offered an apologetic smile. “I was thinking of a good friend. He...” Suddenly he asked, “Isn't the education commissioner's office at Jiangyin?”

zh: “我倒不大清楚。”那人答道：“江苏的大官儿最多，真搞不清什么衙门在什么地方？”
en: “I'm not sure,” the man replied. “Jiangsu has so many high officials that I can never remember which office is where.”

zh: “怎么搞不清。”邻桌上有人答话，“不错，江苏的大官最多，不过衙门都在好地方。”他屈着手指数道：“从情江浦开始数好了，南河总督驻清江浦，漕运总督驻淮安，两江总督、驻防将军、江宁藩司驻江宁，江苏巡抚、江苏藩司驻苏州，学政驻江阴，两淮盐政驻扬州。”
en: “How can you not know?” someone at the next table interjected. “Jiangsu certainly has the most high officials, but all their offices are in fine places.” He counted them on his fingers. “Start with Qingjiangpu. The southern river governor-general is here; the director-general of grain transport is at Huai'an. The governor-general of Liangjiang, the garrison general, and the Jiangning provincial treasurer are at Jiangning. The governor and provincial treasurer of Jiangsu are at Suzhou; the education commissioner is at Jiangyin; and the Lianghuai salt commissioner is at Yangzhou.”

zh: 果然是在江阴。王有龄心里在盘算，由运河到了扬州，不妨沿江东去，到江阴看一看何桂清，然后再经无锡、苏州、嘉兴回杭州，也还不迟。
en: So Jiangyin it was. Wang began planning. Once he reached Yangzhou by canal, he could travel east along the river to visit He Guiqing, then return to Hangzhou by way of Wuxi, Suzhou, and Jiaxing. There would still be time.

zh: 刚刚盘算停当，高升气喘吁吁地寻了来了，他好不容易才觅着一间房，虽丢了定钱在那里，去迟了保不定又为他人所得，兵荒马乱，无处讲理，所以催着主人快走。
en: He had just settled the plan when Gao returned, out of breath. After great difficulty, he had found a room. Though he had left a deposit, someone else might take it if they delayed. In the confusion of war there would be no one to whom they could appeal, so he urged his master to hurry.

zh: 于是王有龄起身付了茶钱，主仆两人走出店来，拦着一名挑伕，把笨重箱笼挑了一担。高升背了铺盖卷，其余帽笼之类的轻便什物，便由王有龄亲手拿着，急匆匆赶到客店。是一间极狭窄的小屋，而且靠近厨房，抽烟弥漫，根本不宜作为客房。可是看到街上那些扶老携幼，彷惶不知何处可以容身的难民，王有龄便觉得这问小屋简直就是天堂了。
en: Wang paid for the tea, and they went outside. They stopped a porter to carry the heavy trunks and cases on a shoulder pole. Gao took the bedding roll on his back, while Wang himself carried the lighter things, including the hat case. They hurried to the inn. The room was tiny and stood beside the kitchen, where cooking smoke filled the air. It was hardly fit for a guest. Yet when Wang thought of the refugees outside, supporting the old and leading children, not knowing where they could shelter, this little room seemed positively heavenly.

zh: “你呢？”他关切地问高升，“也得找个铺才好。”
en: “What about you?” he asked Gao with concern. “You need somewhere to sleep too.”

zh: “我就在老爷床前打地铺。反正雇好了船就走，也不过天把的事。”
en: “I'll spread my bedding on the floor beside your bed. We'll leave as soon as we've hired a boat. It'll only be a day or so.”

zh: “高升！我想绕到江阴去看一看何大人。”王有龄把他的打算说了出来。
en: “Gao Sheng, I'd like to make a detour to Jiangyin to see His Excellency He.” Wang explained his plan.

zh: “这个……”高升迟疑地答道：“我劝老爷还是一直回杭州的好，一则要早早禀到，二则多换两次船，在平常不费事，这几天可是很大的麻烦。老爷，消息很不好，万一路断了，怎么办？“
en: “Well...” Gao hesitated. “I would advise going straight back to Hangzhou. For one thing, you should report your arrival as soon as possible. For another, changing boats twice more would be easy enough in ordinary times, but it could be very troublesome now. The news is bad, sir. What if the route is cut off?”

zh: 高升的见识着实不低，分发浙江的候补州县，如果归路中断，逗留在江苏，那是一辈子都补不到缺的，所以王有龄一听他的放，翻然变计，当夜商量定规，尽快雇船赶回浙江。
en: Gao's judgement was sound. An expectant magistrate assigned to Zhejiang could wait for ever without obtaining a post if he became stranded in Jiangsu. Wang changed his mind at once. That evening they agreed to hire a boat and reach Zhejiang as quickly as possible.

zh: 第二天早晨一看，难民已到了许多，同时也有了确实消息，芜湖已经失守，官军水师大败，福山镇总兵阵亡，洪杨军正分水陆三路，进薄江宁。江南的老百姓，一二百年未经兵革，恐慌万状，因而雇船也不容易，南面战火弥漫，船家既怕送人虎口，又怕官府抓差扣船，不管哪一样，反正遇上了就要大倒其霉。
en: By the next morning, many more refugees had arrived, along with definite news. Wuhu had fallen, the government fleet had suffered a crushing defeat, and the brigade commander of Fushan had been killed. Hong and Yang's forces were advancing on Jiangning in three columns by land and water. The people of the lower Yangtze region, who had known no warfare for a century or two, were panic-stricken. Hiring a boat was difficult. With war spreading through the south, boatmen feared both taking their passengers into danger and having their vessels requisitioned by the authorities. Either could mean disaster.

zh: 奔走了一天，总算有了结果，有一批浙江的漕船回空，可以附搭便客，论人计价，每人二十两银子，这比平时贵了十倍不止，事急无奈，王有龄惟有忍痛点头。
en: After a day's searching, they finally found a solution. Some Zhejiang grain boats were returning empty and could take passengers, at twenty taels a head. This was more than ten times the usual fare. With no alternative in such urgency, Wang reluctantly agreed.

zh: 但也亏得是坐漕船，一路上“讨关”、“过坝”可得许多方便。风向也顺，船行极快，到了扬州，听说江宁已经被围，城外有七八十万头裹红中的太平军，城里只有四千旗兵，一千绿营兵，不过明太祖兴建的江宁城，坚固有名，一时不易攻下。
en: Still, travelling on a grain boat brought advantages at checkpoints and dams. The wind was favourable, and they made rapid progress. At Yangzhou they heard that Jiangning was under siege. Outside its walls stood seven or eight hundred thousand Taiping soldiers with red cloths wrapped around their heads; inside were only four thousand banner troops and a thousand Green Standard soldiers. The walls built by the founding Ming emperor were famously strong, however, and would not be easily breached.

zh: 如果真的有七八十万人，洪杨军能不能攻下江宁，无关大局。王有龄心里在想，他们的兵力足够，分兵两路，一去往东，径取苏常，一支渡江而北，经营中原，这一来江宁成了孤城，不战自下。由于这个想法，王有龄对大局相当悲观，中宵不寐，听着运河的水声，心潮起伏，不知如何才能挽救江南的劫运？
en: If the attackers really numbered seven or eight hundred thousand, Wang thought, whether they took Jiangning immediately was almost beside the point. They had enough men to divide their forces: one army could advance east and seize Suzhou and Changzhou, while another crossed north of the river to establish itself on the Central Plain. Jiangning would then become an isolated city and fall without a battle. The thought made him pessimistic about the wider situation. Lying awake at midnight, listening to the canal water, he turned over the question of how the lower Yangtze region might be saved from disaster.

zh: 就这样忧心忡仲地到了杭州。一上岸第一个想别的不是家，是胡雪岩，但自然没有行装未卸，便上茶馆里去寻他的道理。而一到了家，却又有许多事要料理，当务之急是寻房子搬家。原来的住处过于狭隘，且莫说排场气派，首先高升就没有地方住，所以他在家只得坐一坐，喝了杯茶，随即带着高升去寻房屋经纪。
en: In this troubled state of mind, he reached Hangzhou. His first thought on landing was not of home but of Hu Xueyan. Yet naturally he could not go searching the teahouses before even putting down his luggage. Once home, he found many things to arrange. Most urgent was a move to a larger house. Their existing quarters were cramped; quite apart from appearances, there was nowhere for Gao to stay. Wang therefore sat only long enough to drink a cup of tea before taking Gao out to find a property agent.

zh: 买卖房屋的经纪人，杭州叫做“瓦摇头”，他们有日常聚会的地方，在一家茶馆，各行各业都有一家茶馆作为买卖联络的集中之处。称为“茶会”。
en: In Hangzhou, property brokers were nicknamed “tile-shakers.” They gathered daily at a particular teahouse. Each trade had such a place where business contacts were made, known as its “tea meeting.”

zh: 到了茶会上，那些连“瓦”见了他们都“摇头”的经纪人，一看王有龄的服饰气派，还带着底下人，都以为是大主顾来了，纷纷上来兜搭，问他是要买呢，还是“典”？
en: When Wang arrived, the brokers—men who supposedly made even roof tiles shake their heads—took one look at his clothes, bearing, and attendant and assumed that an important customer had appeared. They crowded round to ask whether he wished to buy a house or take possession of one under a mortgage arrangement.

zh: “我既不买，也不典。想租一宅房子。而且要快，最好今天就能搬进去。”
en: “Neither. I want to rent a house, and quickly. Ideally, I should like to move in today.”

zh: “这哪里来？”大家都有些失望地笑了。
en: “Where would you find that?” they laughed, somewhat disappointed.

zh: “我有。”有个人说。
en: “I have one,” a man said.

zh: 于是王有龄只与此人谈交易，问了房子的格局，大小恰如所砍，再问租金，也还不贵，“那就去看一看再说。”王有龄这样表示，“看定了立刻成约，当日起租。我做事喜欢痛快，疙里疙瘩的房子我可不要。”
en: Wang turned to negotiate with him alone. The layout sounded exactly right, and the rent was reasonable. “Then let's go and look,” Wang said. “If it suits me, we'll make the agreement at once and the tenancy can begin today. I like things straightforward. I don't want a house with complications attached.”

zh: 听你老人家是福建口音夹杭州口音，想必也吃了好几年西湖水，难道还不知道‘杭铁头’说一下二？“
en: “From your accent, I'd say you're from Fujian but have lived in Hangzhou for some years. Surely you know that we stubborn Hangzhou men stand by our word?”

zh: 那房子在清和坊，这一带杭州称为“上城”，从南宋以来，就是一城精华所在，离佑圣观巷的抚台衙门和藩司前的藩台衙门都不远，“上院”方便，先就中王有龄的意。再看房子，五开间的正屋，一共两进，左右厢房，前面轿厅，后面还有一片竹林，盖着个小小的亭子，虽不富丽，也下寒酸，正台王有龄现在的身分。
en: The house was in Qinghefang, in the district Hangzhou called the Upper City. Since the Southern Song, this had been the heart of the town. It was close to both the governor's office in Youshengguan Lane and the provincial treasury, making official visits convenient. That alone pleased Wang. The house itself had a main building five bays wide, two successive courtyards, side wings, a sedan-chair hall at the front, and a small pavilion in a bamboo grove behind. Neither luxurious nor shabby, it suited his present standing perfectly.

zh: 看到他的脸色，“瓦摇头”便说：“王老爷鸿运高照！原住的张老爷调升山西，昨天刚刚动身。这么好的房子，一天都不会空，就不定明天就租了出去，偏偏王老爷就是今天来看，真正巧极了！”
en: Reading his expression, the broker said, “Your Honour's luck is certainly flourishing. The previous tenant, Mr Zhang, was promoted and transferred to Shanxi. He left only yesterday. A house like this won't stay empty even a day; it might be let tomorrow. And you happen to come today. What a fortunate coincidence!”

zh: “是啊，巧得很！”王有龄也觉得事事顺遂，十分高兴，“你马上去找房东，此刻就订约起租。”
en: “Yes, very fortunate!” Wang too felt that everything was going his way. Delighted, he said, “Find the landlord immediately. We'll sign the agreement and begin the tenancy now.”

zh: “老爷！”高升插嘴问道：“哪一天搬进来？”
en: “When shall we move in, sir?” Gao asked.

zh: “拣日不如撞日，今天就搬，万一来不及就是明天。”
en: “No day is better than the day at hand. Today, if we can; otherwise tomorrow.”

zh: 这一天是无论如何来不及了，但也有许多事要做，第一步先雇人来打扫房子，第二步要买动用家具，为了不愿意露出暴发户的味道，王有龄特地买了半旧的红木桌椅，加上原有的一套，从云南带来的大理石的茶几、椅子，铺陈开来，显得很够气派。
en: Moving that day proved impossible, but there was plenty to do. First, men had to be hired to clean the house; then furniture and household necessities had to be bought. Wishing to avoid the air of a man suddenly come into money, Wang deliberately chose used mahogany tables and chairs. Together with his existing set of marble tables and chairs brought from Yunnan, they made an impressive display.

zh: 真个“有钱好办事”，搬到新居，不过两天工夫，诸事妥贴，厨房里厨子，上房里丫头、老妈，门房里坐着四个轿班，轿厅里停一顶簇新的蓝呢轿子。高升便是他的大管家。
en: Money did indeed make things easy. Within two days of the move, everything was arranged: a cook in the kitchen, maids and an older woman in the private rooms, four chair-bearers waiting in the gatehouse, and a brand-new blue-cloth sedan chair in the front hall. Gao had become his chief steward.

zh: 这就该去寻胡雪岩了。王有龄觉得现在身分虽与前不同，但不可炫濯于患难之交，所以这天早晨，穿了件半旧棉袍，也不带底下人，安步当车，踱到了以前每日必到的那家茶馆。自然遇到很多熟人，却独独不见胡雪岩。
en: It was time to look for Hu Xueyan. Though his position had changed, Wang felt he must not flaunt it before a friend who had stood by him in poverty. One morning he put on a worn padded robe, took no servant, and walked to the teahouse he had once visited every day. He met many familiar faces there, but not Hu.

zh: “小胡呢？”他问茶博士。
en: “Where's Young Hu?” he asked the tea attendant.

zh: “好久没有来了。”
en: “He hasn't been here for a long time.”

zh: “咦！”王有龄心里有些着急，“怎么回事？到哪里去了？”
en: “Why?” Wang grew anxious. “What's happened? Where has he gone?”

zh: “不晓得。”茶博士摇摇头，“这个人神出鬼没，哪个也弄不清楚他的事。”
en: “No idea.” The attendant shook his head. “He comes and goes like a spirit. Nobody really knows his affairs.”

zh: “这样……”王有龄要了张包茶叶的纸，借支笔写了自己的地址，交给茶博士，郑重嘱咐：“如果遇见小胡，千万请他到我这里来。”
en: “Well, then...” Wang asked for a piece of tea-wrapping paper, borrowed a brush, and wrote down his address. Handing it over, he said earnestly, “If you see him, please be sure to ask him to come to me.”

zh: 走出茶馆，想想不放心，怕茶博士把他的话置诸脑后，特为又回进去，取块两把重的碎银子，塞到茶博士千里。
en: After leaving, he remained uneasy. Afraid that the attendant might forget, he went back and pressed a piece of broken silver weighing about two taels into the man's hand.

zh: “咦！咦！为啥？”
en: “Oh! What's this for?”

zh: “我送你的。你替我寻一寻小胡，寻着了我再谢你。”
en: “It's for you. Help me find Young Hu, and I'll thank you again when you do.”

zh: 那茶博士有些发愣，心想这姓王的，以前一壶茶要冲上十七八回开水，中午两个烧饼当顿饭，如今随便出手就是两把银子，想来发了财了！可是看看他的服饰又不象怎么有钱，居然为了寻小胡，不惜整两银子送人，其中必有道理。
en: The attendant was astonished. This Mr Wang had once asked for his tea to be topped up seventeen or eighteen times and made a midday meal of two flatbreads. Now he casually handed over two taels of silver. He must have made money. Yet his clothes did not suggest much wealth. There had to be some reason why he was willing to spend two whole taels merely to find Young Hu.

zh: “这，这……真不好意思了。”茶博士问道，“不过我要请教你老人家，为啥寻小胡？”
en: “Well, I... this is too generous.” The attendant asked, “But may I know why you're looking for him, sir?”

zh: “要好朋友嘛！”王有龄笑笑不说下去了。
en: “He's a good friend.” Wang smiled and said no more.

zh: 作了这番安排，他怅惘的心情略减，相信那茶博士一天到晚与三教九流的人打交谊，眼皮宽，人头熟，只要肯留心访查，一定可以把小胡寻着。只怕小胡来访，不易找到地址，所以一回家便叫人去买了一张梅红笺，大书“闽候王有龄寓”六字，贴在门上。
en: Having made these arrangements, he felt less disappointed. The attendant dealt all day with people from every walk of life and had a wide circle of acquaintances. If he made a real effort, he would surely find Hu. Wang's remaining fear was that Hu might have difficulty finding the house. As soon as he returned, he sent for a sheet of plum-red paper, wrote “Residence of Wang Youling of Minhou” in large characters, and had it pasted on the gate.

zh: 这就要预备禀到、投信了。未上藩署以前，他先要到按察使衙门去看一个朋友。按察使通称桌司，尊称力桌台，掌管一省的刑名。王有龄的那个朋友就是臬司衙门的“刑名师爷”，姓俞，绍兴人。“绍兴师爷”遍布十八行省、大小衙门，所以有句“无绍不成衙”的俗语，尤其是州县官，一成了缺，第一件大事就是延聘“刑名”、“钱谷”两幕友，请到了好手，才能一帆顺风，名利双收。
en: He now had to prepare to report his arrival and deliver his letter. Before visiting the provincial treasury, he wished to see a friend at the judicial commissioner's office. The provincial judicial commissioner, commonly called the niesi and respectfully the nietai, supervised criminal justice throughout the province. Wang's friend, a man surnamed Yu from Shaoxing, was the office's legal adviser. Shaoxing secretaries worked in government offices great and small throughout the eighteen provinces, giving rise to the saying, “No Shaoxing men, no government office.” For a local magistrate in particular, the first task on receiving a post was to engage advisers for criminal justice and revenue. With capable men in both positions, his administration could run smoothly and bring him reputation and wealth.

zh: 王有龄的这个朋友，就是刑名好手，不但一部《大清律》倒背如流，肚子里还藏着无数的案例。向来刑名案子，有律讲律，无律讲例，只要有例可援，定漱的文卷，报到刑部都不会被驳。江浙桌台衙门的“俞师爷”，就是连刑部司官都知道其人的，等闲不会驳他经办的案子，所以历任臬司都要卑词厚币，挽留他“帮忙”。
en: Wang's friend was an outstanding legal adviser. He knew the Great Qing Code backwards and carried countless precedents in his head. In criminal cases, one applied the statute where there was one and relied on precedent where there was none. With a precedent to support the decision, the case papers sent to the Board of Punishments would not be rejected. “Secretary Yu” of the provincial judicial offices in Jiangsu and Zhejiang was known even to officials at that Board. They rarely questioned cases he had handled. Successive judicial commissioners therefore retained him with flattering words and generous pay.

zh: 俞师爷的叔叔曾在福建“游幕”，与王有龄也是总角之交，但平日不甚往来。这天见他登门相访，料知“无事不登三宝殿”，便率直问道：“雪轩兄，何事见教？”
en: Yu's uncle had served on private official staffs in Fujian, and Yu and Wang had known each other since childhood, though they seldom met. Seeing Wang arrive that day, Yu assumed he had come for a reason and asked directly, “Brother Xuexuan, what brings you here?”

zh: “有两件事想跟老兄来请教。”王有龄说，“你知道的，我本来捐了个盐大使，去年到京里走了一趟，过了班，分发本省。”
en: “There are two matters on which I'd like your advice,” Wang replied. “You know I had purchased qualification as a salt-station superintendent. Last year I went to the capital, changed categories, and obtained assignment to this province.”

zh: 盐大使“过班”，自然是州县班子，俞师爷原来也捐了个八品官儿，好为祖宗三代请“诰封”，这时见王有龄官比自己大了，便慢吞吞地拉长了绍兴腔说。“恭喜，恭喜！我要喊你‘大人’了。”
en: For a salt-station superintendent, changing categories naturally meant qualifying for a local magistracy. Yu himself had purchased an eighth-rank title so that he could secure imperial honours for three generations of his ancestors. Now that Wang outranked him, he drawled in his Shaoxing accent, “Congratulations! I shall have to call you ‘Your Excellency.’”

zh: “老朋友何苦取笑。”王有龄问道：“我请问，椿藩台那件案子现在怎么了？”
en: “Why tease an old friend? Tell me, what's happening with Provincial Treasurer Chunshou's case?”

zh: “你也晓得这件案子！”俞师爷又间一句：“你可知道黄抚台的来头？”
en: “So you know about that affair too!” Yu asked another question. “Do you know who stands behind Governor Huang?”

zh: “略略知道些。他的同年，在朝里势力大得很。”
en: “A little. His examination classmates are very powerful at court.”

zh: “那就是了，何必再问？”
en: “Exactly. Why ask any more?”

zh: “不过我听说京里派了钦差来查。可有这事？”
en: “But I heard that an imperial commissioner had been sent to investigate. Is that true?”

zh: “查不查都是一样。”俞师爷说，“就是查，也是自己人来查。”
en: “It makes no difference whether there's an investigation,” Yu said. “If there is one, it'll be conducted by one of their own.”

zh: 听这口意，王有龄明白他意何所指？自己不愿把跟何桂清的关系说破，那就无法深谈了。但有一点必须打听一下：“那么，那个‘自己人’到杭州来过没有？”
en: Wang understood the implication. He did not wish to reveal his connection with He Guiqing, so he could not pursue the discussion openly. But there was one thing he needed to know. “Has this person of their own been to Hangzhou yet?”

zh: “咦！”俞师爷极注意地看着他，“雪轩兄，你知道得不少啊！”
en: “Oh!” Yu looked at him closely. “You seem to know quite a lot, Brother Xuexuan.”

zh: “哪里。原是特意来请教。”
en: “Not at all. That's why I've come to ask you.”

zh: 俞师爷沉吟了一会放低声音说：“既是老朋友，你来问我，我不能不说，不过这一案关系抚台的前程，话不好乱传，得罪了抚台犯不着。你问的话如果与你无关，最好不必去管这闲事，是为明哲保身之道。”
en: After a moment's thought, Yu lowered his voice. “Since we're old friends and you've asked, I cannot refuse to answer. But the governor's future depends on this case. One mustn't spread stories carelessly; offending him would gain nothing. If the matter does not concern you, it's best to leave it alone. That's the sensible way to keep yourself safe.”

zh: 听俞师爷这么说，王有龄不能没有一个确实的回答，但要“为贤者讳”，不肯直道他与何桂清的关系，只说，托人求了何桂情的一封“八行”，不知道黄宗汉会不会买帐？
en: Wang now had to give a definite explanation. Wishing to protect the reputation of a man he respected, however, he would not state his relationship with He plainly. He merely said that he had obtained a letter from He through an intermediary and did not know whether Huang would honour it.

zh: “原来如此！恭喜，恭喜，一定买帐。”
en: “So that's it! Congratulations! He certainly will.”

zh: “何以见得？”
en: “How can you be sure?”

zh: “老实告诉你！”俞师爷说：“何学台已经来过了。隔省的学政，无缘无故怎么跑到浙江来？怕引起外头的猜嫌，于黄抚台的官声不利，所以行踪极其隐秘。好在他是奉旨密查，这么做也不算不对。你想，何学台如此回护他的老同年，黄抚台对他的‘八行’，岂有不买帐之礼？”
en: “I'll tell you frankly. Education Commissioner He has already been here. Why should an education commissioner from another province suddenly come to Zhejiang? His visit might arouse suspicion and harm Governor Huang's reputation, so his movements were kept extremely secret. Fortunately, his orders were to investigate secretly, so that was not in itself improper. Think of it: if He has gone to such lengths to protect his old examination classmate, how could Huang fail to honour a letter from him?”

zh: “啊！”王有龄不由得笑了，他一直有些患得患夫之心，怕伺、黄二人的交情，并不如何往清自己所说的那么深厚，现在从旁人口中说出来，可以深信不疑了。
en: “Ah!” Wang could not help smiling. He had been anxious, afraid that the friendship was less close than He himself claimed. Now that someone else had confirmed it, he could believe it without reservation.

zh: “再告诉你句话：黄抚台奉旨查问，奏复上去，说椿寿‘因库款不敷，漕务棘手，致肝疾举发，因而自尽，并无别情’。这‘并无别情’四个字，岂是随便说得的？只要有了‘别情’，不问‘别情’为何，皆是‘欺罔’的大罪，不杀头也得坐牢，全靠何学台替他隐瞒，你想想看，这是替他担了多大的干系？“
en: “Let me tell you something else,” Yu continued. “When ordered to investigate, Huang reported that Chunshou, ‘distressed by the shortage of treasury funds and the difficulties of grain transport, suffered an attack of liver disease and consequently took his own life; there were no other circumstances.’ Can a man write those last words lightly? If there were any other circumstances, whatever they might be, he would be guilty of deceiving the throne. If he escaped execution, he would still go to prison. He is relying entirely on Commissioner He to conceal the truth. Just consider how much responsibility He has assumed on his behalf.”

zh: 一听这活，王有龄倒有些替何桂清担心，因为帮着隐瞒，便是同犯“欺罔”之罪，一里事发，也是件不得了的事。
en: This made Wang anxious for He Guiqing. Helping to conceal the truth meant sharing the guilt of deceiving the emperor. If the affair came to light, the consequences would be disastrous.

zh: 俞师爷再厉害，也猜不到他这一桩心事，只是为老朋友高兴，拍着他的肩说，“你快上院投信去吧！包你不到十天，藩司就会‘挂牌’放缺。到那时候，我好好荐个同乡给你办刑名。”
en: For all his shrewdness, Yu could not guess this concern. He was simply pleased for his old friend and patted him on the shoulder. “Go and deliver the letter at once. I guarantee the provincial treasury will post your appointment within ten days. When that happens, I'll recommend a good fellow from my home district to handle your legal work.”

zh: “对了！”王有龄急忙拱手称谢，“这件事非仰仗老兄不可，刑、钱两友，都要请老兄替我物色。”
en: “Exactly!” Wang hurriedly clasped his hands in thanks. “I shall have to rely on you for that. Please find me both a legal and a revenue adviser.”

zh: “有，有！都在我身上。快办正事去吧！”
en: “Certainly. Leave it all to me. Now go and attend to your business.”

zh: 于是王有龄当天就上藩署禀到，递上手本，封了四两银子的“门包”。
en: That same day, Wang reported to the provincial treasury, submitting his visiting card with four taels of silver wrapped as a gratuity for the gatekeepers.

zh: 候补州县无其数，除非有大来头，藩司不会单独接见，王有龄也知道这个规矩，不过因为照道理必应有此一举，所以听得门上从里面回出来，说声：“上头身子不舒服，改日请王老爷来谈。”随即道了劳，转身而去。
en: Expectant magistrates were innumerable. Unless a man had powerful backing, the provincial treasurer would not receive him individually. Wang knew this rule, but propriety required him to make the attempt. When the gatekeeper returned with the message, “His Excellency is unwell and will invite you to call another day,” Wang thanked him for his trouble and left.

zh: 蓝呢轿子由藩同前抬到佑对观巷抚台衙门，轿班一看照墙下停了好几顶绿呢大轿，不敢乱闯，远远地就停了下来，工有龄下了轿，跟高升交换了一个眼色，一前一后，走入大门。抚台衙门的门上，架子特别大，一看王有龄的“顶戴”，例知是个候补州县，所以等高升从拜匣里拿出手本递去，连正眼郁不着他，喊一声，“小八子，登门簿！”
en: His blue-cloth chair carried him from the treasury to the governor's office in Youshengguan Lane. Seeing several large green-cloth chairs beside the screen wall, the bearers dared not approach and stopped some distance away. Wang got out, exchanged a glance with Gao, and entered ahead of him. The governor's gatekeepers were particularly high-handed. One look at Wang's hat insignia told them he was an expectant magistrate. When Gao took his card from its case and offered it, a gatekeeper did not even look properly at him, but called, “Little Eight! Enter him in the callers' register!”

zh: 那个被呼为“小八子”的，是个眉清目秀的少年，但架子也下小，向高升说道，“把手本拿过来！”
en: The youth addressed as Little Eight had delicate features but no shortage of arrogance. “Bring the card here,” he told Gao.

zh: 在藩台衙门，手本辽往里递一递，在这里连手本都是白费，好在高升是见过世面的，不慌不忙摸出个门包；递了给门上，他接在手里掂了掂，脸色略略好看了些，问一句：“贵上尊姓？”
en: At the treasury, at least the card had been taken inside. Here, even submitting it seemed pointless. Gao, however, knew the world. Calmly he produced a gratuity and handed it to the gatekeeper. The man weighed it in his hand, looked slightly less forbidding, and asked, “Your master's surname?”

zh: “敝上姓王！”高升把何桂清的信取出来：“有封信，拜托递一递。”
en: “Wang.” Gao took out He Guiqing's letter. “There is also a letter. Would you be so good as to deliver it?”

zh: 看在门包的分上，那门上似乎万般无奈地说：“好了，好了，替你去跑一趟。”
en: In consideration of the gratuity, the gatekeeper replied as though yielding reluctantly, “Very well, very well. I'll take it in for you.”

zh: 他懒洋洋地地站起身，顺手抓了顶红缨帽戴在头上，一直往里走去。抚台衙门地方甚大，光是中间那条甬道就要走好半天，王有龄便耐心等着。但这一等的时间实在太久了，不但他们主仆忐忑不安，连门房里的人也都诧异：“怎么回事，刘二爷进去了这半天还不出来？”
en: He rose languidly, picked up a red-tasselled hat, put it on, and went inside. The governor's compound was extensive; the central passage alone took a considerable time to traverse. Wang waited patiently. Yet the delay became so long that not only master and servant grew uneasy; even the men in the gatehouse were puzzled. “What's happened? Second Master Liu has been in there ages.”

zh: “也许上头有别的事交代。”
en: “Perhaps His Excellency has other instructions for him.”

zh: 这是个合理的猜测，王有龄听在耳朵里，凉了半截，黄宗汉根本就不理何桂清的信，更没有把自己放在眼里！否则决不会把等候谒见的人，轻搁在一边，管自己去交代别的事。
en: That was a reasonable guess, but it chilled Wang's hopes. Huang must have ignored He's letter and attached no importance to him. Otherwise, why leave a man awaiting an audience while giving instructions about something else?

zh: “刘二爷出来了！”高升悄悄说道。
en: “Second Master Liu is coming out,” Gao said quietly.

zh: 王有龄抬眼一望，便觉异样，刘二已泅不似刚迸去时的那种一步懒似一步的神情，如今是脚步匆速，而且双眼望着自己这面，仿佛有什么紧要消息急于来通知似地。
en: Wang looked up and noticed the change at once. Liu no longer moved with his earlier indolence. He was hurrying, his eyes fixed in their direction, as though eager to communicate important news.

zh: 这一下，他也精神一振，且迎着刘二，只见他奔到面前，先请了个安，含笑说道：“王大老爷！请门房里坐。”
en: Wang's spirits rose. He turned towards Liu, who came straight to him, made a respectful salute, and smiled. “Your Honour Wang! Please come and sit in the gatehouse.”

zh: 何前倔而后恭？除掉王有龄主仆，门房里的，还有一直在那里的闲人，无不投以惊异的神色，有些就慢慢地跟了过来，想打听一下，这位戴“水晶顶子”的七品官儿，是何来历？连抚台衙门赫赫有名的刘二爷都对他这样客气？
en: Why this change from arrogance to deference? Apart from Wang and Gao, everyone in the gatehouse and all the idlers nearby looked astonished. Some drifted closer, hoping to learn who this seventh-rank official with a crystal hat button might be. Even the governor's celebrated Second Master Liu was treating him with extraordinary courtesy.

zh: 等进了门房，刘二奉他上坐，倒上茶来，亲手捧过去，一面间道：“王大老爷公馆在哪里？”
en: Inside, Liu gave Wang the best seat, poured tea, and presented it himself. “Where is Your Honour's residence?” he asked.

zh: “在清和坊。”王有龄说了地址，刘二叫人记了下来。
en: “In Qinghefang.” Wang supplied the address, and Liu had someone write it down.

zh: “是这样，”他说，“上头交代，说手本暂时留下，此刻司道都在，请王大老爷进去，只怕没有工夫细谈。今天晚上请王大老爷过来吃个便饭，也不必穿公服。回头另外送帖子到公馆里去！”
en: “This is the situation,” he said. “His Excellency asks to keep your card for now. The commissioners and intendants are with him at present, and if he invited you in, he fears there would be no time for a proper conversation. He would like you to dine here this evening. There is no need for formal dress. An invitation will be sent to your residence shortly.”

zh: “喔，喔！”王有龄从容答道，“抚台太客气了！”
en: “Oh, indeed.” Wang answered composedly, “The governor is most kind.”

zh: “上头又说，王大老爷是同乡世交，不便照一般的规矩接见。晚上请早些过来，我在这里伺候，请贵管家找刘二接贴就是了。”
en: “He also said that you are a fellow provincial and an old family connection, and should not be received by the ordinary rules. Please come early this evening. I shall be here. Your steward need only ask for Liu Er.”

zh: 高升这时正站在门外，听他这一说，便悄悄走了进去，王有龄看见了喊道，“高升，你来见见刘二爷。”
en: Gao was standing outside the door. Hearing this, he quietly came in. Wang saw him and said, “Gao Sheng, come and pay your respects to Second Master Liu.”

zh: “刘二爷！”高升请了个安。
en: “Second Master Liu!” Gao made a salute.

zh: 刘二回了礼。跟班听差，客气些都称“二爷”，所以刘二不管他行几，回他一声：“高二爷！”又说，“都是自己人，有什么事只管招呼我，不必客气！”
en: Liu returned it. Servants were politely addressed as “Second Master” regardless of their actual place among their brothers, so he replied, “Second Master Gao!” Then he added, “We're all friends here. If you need anything, just let me know. There's no need for ceremony.”

zh: “是，是！将来麻烦刘二爷的地方一定很多，请多关照。”
en: “Thank you. I'm sure we'll have much to trouble you with in future. We shall be grateful for your help.”

zh: 这时王有龄已站起身，刘二便喊：“看！王大老爷的轿子在那里，快抬过来。”
en: Wang had risen. Liu called out, “Where is His Honour Wang's chair? Bring it over at once!”

zh: 他的那顶蓝呢大轿、一直停在西辕门外，等抬到大门，王有龄才踱着八字步，走了出去，刘二哈着腰亦步亦趋地跟在后面。那些司道的从人轿班，看刘二比伺候“首县”还要巴结，无不侧目而视，窃窃私议。
en: It had been waiting outside the western outer gate. Only when it reached the main entrance did Wang walk out with the measured gait of an official, Liu following close behind with a deferential bend of the body. The servants and bearers of the commissioners and intendants watched sideways and whispered. Liu was being more attentive than he was even to the magistrate of the provincial capital's principal county.

zh: 回家不久，果然送来一份黄宗汉的请帖，王有龄自然准时赴宴。虽然刘二已预先关照，只开便衣，他却不敢把抚台的客气话当真，依旧穿公服，备手本，只不过叫高升带着衣包备用。
en: Soon after Wang returned home, Huang's invitation arrived. He naturally went at the appointed hour. Although Liu had said that ordinary clothes would suffice, Wang did not dare take the governor's politeness literally. He wore formal robes and prepared a visiting card, merely asking Gao to bring a change of clothes.

zh: 到了扰台商门下轿，刘二已经等在那里、随限把他领到西花厅，说一声：“王大老爷请坐，等我到上面去回。”
en: Liu was waiting when his chair arrived at the governor's office. He led Wang to the western reception room. “Please sit down, Your Honour. I'll announce you.”

zh: 没有多少时候，听得靠里一座通上房的侧门外面，有人咳嗽，随后便进来一个听差，一手托着银水烟袋，一手打开棉门帘，王有龄知道黄宗汉出来，随即站起，必恭必敬地立在下方。
en: Before long, a cough sounded beyond a side door leading to the private quarters. An attendant appeared, carrying a silver water pipe in one hand and lifting the padded curtain with the other. Knowing that Huang was coming, Wang rose immediately and stood respectfully at the lower end of the room.

zh: 黄宗汉穿的是便衣，驴脸狮鼻，两颊凹了下去，那双眼睛顾盼之，看到什么就是死盯一眼，一望而知是个极难伺候的人物。王有龄不敢怠慢，趋跄数步，迎面跪了下去，报乞请安。
en: Huang wore informal clothes. He had a long face, a broad nose, and sunken cheeks. As his eyes moved about, they fixed hard upon whatever they noticed. One glance was enough to show that he would be difficult to serve. Wang dared not delay. He hurried forward, knelt, announced his name, and paid his respects.

zh: “不敢当，不敢当！”黄字汉还了个揖，他那听差便来扶起客人。
en: “Please, there is no need!” Huang returned a bow, and his attendant came forward to raise the guest.

zh: 主人非常客气，请客人“升炕”，王有龄谦辞不敢，斜着身子在下方一张椅子上坐下。黄宗汉隔一张茶几坐在上首相陪。
en: The host courteously invited him to sit on the heated platform. Wang declined and took a chair in the less honoured position, sitting with his body turned slightly sideways in deference. Huang sat above him, a small tea table between them.

zh: “我跟根云，在同年中感情最好。雪轩兄既是根云的总角之交，那就跟自己人一样，何况又是同乡，不必拘泥俗礼！”
en: “Of all my examination classmates, Genyun is my closest friend. Since you and he have been friends from childhood, Brother Xuexuan, you are one of us. And we come from the same province. There is no need to be bound by ordinary ceremony.”

zh: “承蒙大人看得起，实在感激，不过礼不可废。”三有龄辩，“一切要求大人教导！”
en: “I am deeply grateful for Your Excellency's kindness,” Wang replied, “but the proper courtesies must be observed. I shall look to you for guidance in everything.”

zh: “哪里！倒是我要借重长才……”
en: “Not at all. It is I who shall have to draw on your abilities...”

zh: 从这里开始，黄宗汉便问他的家世经历，谈了一会，听差来请示开席，又说陪客已经到了。
en: From there, Huang began asking about his family and experience. After a while, an attendant came to ask whether dinner should be served and reported that the other guests had arrived.

zh: “那就请吧！”主人起身肃容，“在席上再谈。”
en: “Then let us go.” The host rose and invited Wang forward. “We can continue at table.”

zh: 走到里间，两位陪客己在等候，都是抚署的“文案”、一个姓朱的管奏折，一个姓秦的管应酬文字。两个人都是举人，会试不利，为黄宗汉邀来帮忙。
en: Two other men were waiting in the inner room. Both were secretaries in the governor's office. One, surnamed Zhu, drafted memorials to the throne; the other, surnamed Qin, handled social correspondence. Both held provincial degrees but had failed at the metropolitan examination, and Huang had invited them to join his staff.

zh: 这一席自然是王有龄首座、怎么样也辞不了的。但论地位，论功名，一个捐班知县高踞在上，总不免局促异常。幸好他读了几部实用的书在肚子里，兼以一路来正赶上洪杨军长驱东下，见闻不同，所以席上谈得很热闹，把那臼惭形秽的感觉掩盖过去了。
en: Wang had no choice but to accept the place of honour at dinner. Yet in both rank and scholarly distinction, a man who had purchased qualification as a county magistrate hardly deserved to sit above the others, and he felt extremely awkward. Fortunately, he had read several practical books and had travelled south just as Hong and Yang's army swept eastward. His unusual experiences and observations kept the conversation lively and helped conceal his sense of inferiority.

zh: 酒列半酣，听差进来向黄宗汉耳边低声说了一句，只听他大声答道：“快拿来！”
en: When the wine had begun to take effect, an attendant came in and whispered in Huang's ear. The governor answered loudly, “Bring it at once!”

zh: 拿来的是一解盖青紫泥大印的公文，拆开来看完，他顺手递了给“朱师爷”。朱师爷却是看不到几行，便皱紧了双眉。
en: What arrived was an official dispatch bearing a large purple seal. Huang opened it, read it, and handed it to Secretary Zhu, whose brows drew together before he had read more than a few lines.

zh: “江宁失守了。”黄宗汉平静地对王有龄说：“这是江苏巡抚来的咨文。”
en: “Jiangning has fallen,” Huang told Wang calmly. “This is a communication from the governor of Jiangsu.”

zh: “果然保不住！”王有龄咽然问道：“两江总督陆大人呢？”
en: “So it could not be held after all!” Wang asked in distress, “What of Governor-General Lu?”

zh: “殉难了。死得冤枉！”黄宗汉说，“长毛用地雷攻破两处城墙，进城以后，上元县刘令，奋勇抵抗，长毛不支，已经退出，不想陆制军从将军署回衙门，遇着溃散的长毛，护勇、轿班，齐轿而逃。陆制军就这么不明不白死在轿子里！唉，大冤枉了！”
en: “He died in the disaster. An unjust death!” Huang said. “The rebels used mines to breach the walls in two places. After they entered, Magistrate Liu of Shangyuan resisted so fiercely that they were already retreating. Unfortunately, Governor-General Lu was returning from the garrison general's office to his own headquarters and encountered some of the fleeing rebels. His guards and chair-bearers abandoned the chair and ran. He died there without even a proper fight. A grievous injustice!”

zh: 黄宗汉表面表现得十分镇静，甚至可说是近乎冷漠，其实是练就了的一套矫情镇物的功夫，他的内心也很紧张，尤其是想到常大淳、蒋文庆、陆建瀛等人，洪杨军一路所经的督抚，纷纷阵亡，地方大吏起居八座，威风权势，非京官可比，但一遇到战乱，守上有责，非与城同存亡不可，象陆建瀛，即使不为洪杨军所杀，能逃出一条命来，也逃不脱革职拿问，丧师失地的罪名，到头来还是难逃一死，恩到这里，黄宗汉不免惊心。
en: Outwardly, Huang remained composed, almost indifferent. This was a practised manner, intended to steady others by concealing his own feelings. Inside, he too was alarmed. He thought of Chang Dachun, Jiang Wenqing, and Lu Jianying: governors and governors-general had died one after another along the rebels' route. Provincial grandees enjoyed splendour, authority, and power far beyond those of officials in the capital. Yet in war they were responsible for their territories and had to stand or fall with their cities. Even had Lu escaped the rebels, he could not have escaped dismissal and investigation for losing troops and territory. Death would still have awaited him. The thought frightened Huang.

zh: 又说了阵时局，行过两巡酒，他忽然问王有龄：“雪轩兄，你的见闻较为真切。照你看，江宁一失，以后如何？”
en: After further discussion of events and two more rounds of wine, he suddenly asked Wang, “Brother Xuexuan, your observations are more direct than ours. Now that Jiangning has fallen, what do you think will happen?”

zh: 王有龄想了想答道：“贼势异常猖獗，而江南防务空虚，加川江南百姓百余年不知兵革，人心浮动，苏、常一带，甚为可虑。”
en: Wang considered before replying. “The rebels are advancing with extraordinary force, while the lower Yangtze region is weakly defended. Its people have known no war for over a century and are deeply unsettled. The area around Suzhou and Changzhou gives particular cause for concern.”

zh: “好在向欣然已经追下来了。自收复武昌以来，八战八克，已拜钦差大臣之命，或许可以收复江宁。”
en: “Fortunately, Xiang Xinran is pursuing them. Since retaking Wuchang, he has won eight victories in eight engagements and has been appointed imperial commissioner. Perhaps he can recover Jiangning.”

zh: 这是秦师爷的意见，王有龄不以为然，但抚署的文案，又是初交，不便驳他，只好微笑不答。
en: This was Secretary Qin's opinion. Wang disagreed, but Qin was a member of the governor's staff and a new acquaintance. It would be awkward to contradict him, so Wang merely smiled.

zh: “我倒要请教，倘或苏常不守，转眼便要侵入本省。雪轩兄，”黄宗汉很注意地看着他，“可能借箸代筹？”
en: “Let me ask this,” Huang continued. “If Suzhou and Changzhou fall, the enemy will soon enter our province. Brother Xuexuan”—he looked closely at Wang—“can you suggest a plan?”

zh: 这带点考问的意思在内，他不敢疏忽。细想一想，从容答道，“洪杨军己成燎原之势，朝廷亦以全力对付，无奈如向帅虽为名将，尚无用武之地，收夏武昌，八战八克，功勋虽高，亦不无因人成事……”
en: There was an element of examination in the question, and Wang dared not answer carelessly. After considering it, he replied calmly, “Hong and Yang's advance has become a spreading fire, and the court is exerting all its strength against it. Yet even a celebrated commander such as General Xiang has had little opportunity to display his abilities. Retaking Wuchang and winning eight successive engagements are great achievements, but they owe something to circumstances created by others...”

zh: “怎么叫‘因人成事’？”黄字汉打断他的话问。
en: “What do you mean by that?” Huang interrupted.

zh: 原是句含蓄的话，既然一定要追问，只好实说。王有龄向秦师爷歉意地笑一笑：“说实在的，洪杨军带着百姓，全军东下，向帅在后面撵，不过收夏了别人的弃地而已。”
en: Wang had intended a tactful hint. Pressed to explain, he had to speak plainly. He smiled apologetically towards Qin. “To tell the truth, Hong and Yang took the civilians with them and moved their whole army east. General Xiang, following behind, has merely recovered places they abandoned.”

zh: “嗯，嗯！”黄宗汉点点头，向秦师爷说：“此论亦不算过苛。”然后又转眼看着王有龄，示意他说下去。
en: “Mm.” Huang nodded and turned to Qin. “That judgement is not unduly harsh.” He then looked back at Wang, inviting him to continue.

zh: “以愚见，如今当苦撑待援，苏常能抵挡得一阵，朝廷一定会调遣精兵，诸路台围，那时候便是个相持的局面，胜负固非一时可决，但局面优势总是稳住了，因此，本省不可等喊临边境，再来出兵，上策莫如出境迎敌！“
en: “In my humble opinion, the immediate task is to hold out until reinforcements arrive. If Suzhou and Changzhou can resist for a time, the court will certainly send its best troops to converge from several directions. A stalemate will follow. Victory may not come quickly, but at least the situation will have been stabilised. Our province should therefore not wait until the enemy reaches its border before sending troops. The best policy is to go beyond our borders and meet them there.”

zh: 黄宗汉凝视着他，突地击案称赏：“好一个‘出境迎敌’！”
en: Huang stared at him, then struck the table in approval. “‘Go beyond our borders and meet them there’—excellent!”

zh: 他在想，出境迎敌，战火便可不致侵入本省，就无所谓“守土之责”，万一吃了败仗，在他入境内，总还有个可以卸责的余地。这还下说，最妙的是，朝廷一再颁示谕旨，不可视他省的战事与己无关，务宜和衷共济，协力防剿，所以出省迎敌正符合上面的意思，等一出奏，必蒙优诏褒答。
en: He was thinking that fighting outside Zhejiang might keep the war from entering the province. His responsibility for defending its territory would then not arise. If his troops were defeated elsewhere, there would still be room to shift the blame. Better still, the court had repeatedly ordered provinces not to regard fighting in other regions as no concern of their own, but to cooperate in defence and suppression. Sending forces across the border would accord perfectly with imperial wishes. A memorial announcing it would surely receive a favourable response.

zh: 专管奏折的朱师爷，也觉得王有龄想出来的这四个字很不坏，大有一番文章可做，也是频频点头。
en: Secretary Zhu, who drafted the memorials, also thought Wang's phrase excellent. There was much to be made of it in writing, and he nodded repeatedly.

zh: 办法是吁！“黄宗汉又说，”不过做起来也不容易。练兵筹饷两事，吃重还在一个饷字！“
en: “The plan is good,” Huang said, “but carrying it out will not be easy. Of the two tasks, training troops and raising military funds, the harder is finding the money.”

zh: “是！”王有龄说：“有土斯有时，有财就有饷，有的就有兵”有兵就有上！“朱师爷接着就了这一句，阑座抚掌大笑。
en: “Indeed,” Wang replied. “With territory comes wealth; with wealth, military funds; with funds, troops.” “And with troops, territory!” Zhu completed the circle. Everyone clapped and laughed.

zh: 于是又谈到筹响之道，王有龄认为保持响源，也就是说，守住宫庶之区最关紧要。然后又谈漕运，他亲身经历过运河的淤浅，感慨着说，时世的推移，只怕己历数千数的河运，将从此没落。而且江南战火已成燎原，运河更难保畅通，所以漕运改为海运，为势所必然，惟有早着先鞭。
en: They discussed ways of raising money. Wang thought it essential to preserve the source of military revenue—that is, to hold the prosperous districts. The conversation then turned to grain transport. Having experienced the canal's shallow, silted channels himself, he remarked that changing times might bring this ancient system into decline. With war spreading through the lower Yangtze region, keeping the canal open would be harder still. A change to sea transport was therefore inevitable, and the sooner preparations began, the better.

zh: 这些议论，他自觉相当平实，黄宗汉和那两位师爷，居然也倾听不倦。
en: He thought these views reasonably practical, and Huang and the two secretaries listened with sustained interest.

zh: 但他忽生警觉，初次谒见抚台，这样子放言高论，不管话说得对不对，总会让入觉得他浮浅狂妄，所以有些失悔，直到终席再不肯多说一句话。
en: Then a warning suddenly occurred to him. This was his first audience with the governor. Whatever the merits of his opinions, speaking so freely and expansively might make him appear shallow and presumptuous. Regretting it, he said almost nothing for the rest of the meal.

zh: 饭扣茗聚，黄宗汉才谈到他的正事，“好在你刚到省。”他说，“且等见了藩司再说。”
en: Over tea afterwards, Huang finally addressed Wang's own business. “Since you've only just returned to the province,” he said, “let us wait until you've seen the provincial treasurer.”

zh: “是！”王有龄低头答道，“总要求大人栽培。”
en: “Yes, Your Excellency.” Wang lowered his head. “I must look to you for advancement.”

zh: “好说，好说！”说着已端起了茶碗。
en: “You are too kind.” As he spoke, Huang lifted his teacup.

zh: 这是对值堂的听差暗示，也就是下逐客令，听差只要一见这个动作，便会拉开嗓子高唱：“送—客—！”
en: This was the signal to the attendant on duty: the interview was over. The moment he saw it, the man called out in a long, loud voice, “Show the guest out!”

zh: 唱到这一声，王有龄慌忙起身请安，黄宗汉送了出来，到堂前请留步，主人不肯，直到花厅门口，再三相拦，黄宗汉才哈一哈腰回身而去。
en: Wang hurriedly rose and saluted. Huang accompanied him towards the door. At the front of the hall, Wang asked him not to come farther, but the host continued. Only after repeated protests at the reception-room doorway did Huang bow slightly and turn back.

zh: 依然是刘二领着出衙问。王有龄心里七上八下，看不出抚台的态度，好象很赏识，又好象是敷衍，极想距刘二打听一下，但要维持宫派，不便跟他在路上谈这事，打算着明干叫高升来探探消息。
en: Liu again led Wang out. Wang was uneasy, unable to judge the governor's attitude. At moments Huang seemed to value him; at others, to be merely polite. He wanted to ask Liu, but maintaining his official dignity made such a conversation on the way out inappropriate. He decided to send Gao to sound things out the next day.

zh: 绕出大堂，就看见簇新两盏“王”字大灯笼，一顶蓝呢轿子都停在门侗里。刘二亲手替他打开轿帘，等他倒退着坐进轿子。才低声说道：“王大老爷请放心，我们大人是这个样子的。要照应人，从不放在嘴上。他自会有话交代藩台。藩台是旗人，讲究礼数，王大老爷不可疏忽！”
en: Beyond the main hall, two new lanterns bearing the character Wang stood beside his blue-cloth chair in the gateway. Liu opened the curtain himself. Only after Wang had backed into his seat did he speak softly. “Rest easy, Your Honour. That's how my master is. When he means to help someone, he doesn't announce it. He'll give instructions to the provincial treasurer. The treasurer is a bannerman and particular about ceremony. Be careful not to overlook anything.”

zh: “是，是！”王有龄在轿中拱手，感激他说，“多亏你照应，承情之至。”
en: “Indeed, indeed!” Wang clasped his hands inside the chair. “I'm deeply grateful for your help.”

zh: 由于有了刘二的那几句话，工有龄这夜才能恬然上床。他自已奇怪，闲了这许多年，也不着急，一旦放缺已有九成把握，反倒左右不放心，这是为了什么？在枕上一个人琢瞎了半天，才悟出其中的道理，他这个官下尽是为自己做，还要有以安慰胡雪岩的期望，所以患得患失之心特甚。
en: Those few words enabled him to go to bed at peace. He wondered at himself: after so many years of idleness without urgency, why was he now anxious on every side when an appointment was almost certain? He pondered it for a long time before understanding. This office was not for himself alone. He also had to fulfil Hu Xueyan's hopes, which made the prospect of success or failure weigh more heavily upon him.

zh: 想起胡雪岩便连带想起一件事，推推枕边人问道：“太太，今天可有人来过？”
en: Thinking of Hu reminded him of something. He nudged his wife beside him. “Did anyone call today?”

zh: “你是问那位胡少爷吗？”王太太是个老实的贤德妇人，“我也是盼望了一天，深怕错过了，叫老妈子一遍一遍到门口去看。没有！没有来过。”
en: “Do you mean Young Master Hu?” His wife was a sincere and kindly woman. “I've been hoping all day too. Afraid we might miss him, I sent the older maid to the gate again and again. But no, he hasn't come.”

zh: “这件事好奇怪……”
en: “It's very strange...”

zh: “都要怪你！”王太太说，“受人这样大的恩惠，竟不问一问人家是什么人家，住在哪里？我看天下的糊涂人，数你为第一了。
en: “It's your own fault,” she said. “After receiving such an immense kindness, you never even asked about his family or where he lived. Of all the muddle-headed people in the world, you must come first.”

zh: “那时也不知道怎么想来的？”王有龄回忆着当时的情形，“事起突然，总有点儿不信其为真，仿佛做了个好梦，只愿这个梦做下去，不愿去追根落实，怕那一来连梦都做不成。”
en: “I don't know what I was thinking.” Wang recalled the occasion. “It happened so suddenly that I could hardly believe it. It was like a wonderful dream. I wanted it to continue and didn't want to examine it too closely, for fear that even the dream would vanish.”

zh: “如果说是做梦，这个梦做得也太希奇，太好了。”王太太欢喜地感叹着，“哪里想得到在通州又遇上那位何大人！”
en: “If it was a dream, it was a very strange and wonderful one,” she said with happy amazement. “Who could have imagined that you would then meet His Excellency He in Tongzhou?”

zh: “是啊！多年音问不通，我从前又不大看那些‘邸报’和进士题名的‘齿录’，竟不知道何桂清如此得意。”王有龄又说，“想想也是，现成有这么好一条路子下去走，守在这里，苦得要命！不好笑吗？”
en: “Exactly. We had lost touch for years, and I never paid much attention to the court gazettes or the biographical registers of successful examination candidates. I had no idea he had done so well.” Wang added, “Just think: such an excellent connection was there all along, and I never used it. Instead, I stayed here in misery. Isn't it ridiculous?”

zh: “现在总算快苦出头了！说来说去，都是老太爷当年种下的善因。就是遇到胡少爷，一定也是老大爷积了阴德。”
en: “At least our hardships are almost over. It all comes back to the good your father did in his lifetime. Even meeting Young Master Hu must have been a reward for his hidden virtue.”

zh: 王有龄深以为然，“公门里面好修行，做州县官，刑名钱谷一把抓，容易造孽，可是也容易积德。老太爷是苦读出身，体恤人情，当年真的做了许多好事。”
en: Wang agreed wholeheartedly. “An official's office offers many opportunities to do good. A local magistrate controls both justice and revenue. It's easy to commit wrongs, but just as easy to accumulate merit. My father knew poverty and hard study, and understood people's difficulties. He really did a great deal of good.”

zh: “你也要学学老太爷，为儿孙种些福田！”王太太又忧郁他说，“受恩不可忘报，现在胡少爷踪影毫无，这件事真急人！”
en: “You must follow his example and plant some blessings for your children and grandchildren.” Then she added anxiously, “And kindness must be repaid. Not knowing where Young Master Hu is makes me very uneasy.”

zh: “唉！”王有龄比她更烦恼，“你不要再说了！说起来我连觉都睡不着。”
en: “Ah!” Wang was even more troubled. “Don't speak of it again. If you do, I won't sleep at all.”

zh: 王太太知道丈夫明日还要起早上藩台衙门，便不再响。到了五更天，悄悄起身，把丫头老妈子都唤醒了。等王有龄起身。一切都已安排得妥妥帖帖，于是吃过早饭，穿戴整齐，坐着轿子，欣然“上院”。
en: Knowing that he had to rise early to visit the provincial treasury, she said no more. Before dawn, she quietly got up and woke the maids and older women. By the time Wang rose, everything was ready. After breakfast, he dressed carefully, entered his chair, and set off in high spirits.

zh: 上院扑了个空，藩司麟桂为漕米海运的事，到上海去了，起码得有十天到半个月的工夫，才能回来，王有龄大为扫兴，只好用“好事多磨”这句话来自宽自解。
en: The visit was fruitless. Provincial Treasurer Lingui had gone to Shanghai on business concerning the sea transport of grain and would not return for at least ten days or a fortnight. Disappointed, Wang could only console himself with the thought that good things seldom came without delays.

zh: 闲着无事，除了每天在家等胡雪岩以外，便是到臬司衙门去访俞师爷，打听时局。京里发来的邪报常有催促各省办理“团练”的上谕，这是仿照嘉庆年间，平“白莲教”时所用的坚壁清野之法，委派各省在籍的大员，本乎“守望相助”的古义，白办乡团练兵，保卫地方，上谕中规定的办法是，除了在籍大员会同地方官，邀集绅士筹办以外，并“着在京各部院堂官及翰、詹、科、道，各举所知，总期通晓事体，居心公正，素系人望者，责成倡办，自必经理得宜，舆情允阶”。同时又训勉办理团练的绅士，说“该绅士等身受厚恩，应如何自固阎里，为敌汽同仇之计，所有劝谕、捐赀、浚濠、筑寨各事，总宜各就地方情形，妥为布置。一切经费，不得令官吏经手。如果办有成效，即由该督抚随时妻请奖励。”
en: With nothing to do, he spent his days either waiting at home for Hu or visiting Secretary Yu to learn the news. The court gazettes frequently carried edicts urging the provinces to organise local militias. The model was the fortified defence and denial of supplies used against the White Lotus rebels during the Jiaqing reign. Senior officials residing in their home provinces were to draw upon the old principle of mutual assistance, organise local forces, and defend their districts. Besides directing these men to work with local officials and gentry, the edicts required senior officials in the capital and members of the academies and censorial offices to recommend people they knew: men who understood affairs, were fair-minded, and already enjoyed public esteem. Entrusted with initiating the work, such men should manage it properly and command public confidence. The gentry were also reminded that, having received imperial favour, they should secure their communities and unite against the enemy. Persuading the population, raising contributions, clearing moats, and building stockades were all to be arranged according to local conditions. No official was to handle the funds. Governors and governors-general could recommend rewards whenever the work proved effective.

zh: “ 你看见没有？”俞师爷指着“一切经费，不得令官吏经手”这句话说，“朝廷对各省地方官，只会刮地皮，不肯实心办事，痛心之情，溢于言表！”
en: “Do you see?” Yu said, pointing to the provision that no official should handle the funds. “The court's distress is plain. Local officials know only how to squeeze the people; they won't work conscientiously.”

zh: “办法是订得不错，有了这句话，绅士不怕掣时，可以放手办事。但凡事以得人为第一，各地的劣绅也不少，如果有意侵渔把持，地方官问一问，便拿上谕来作个挡箭牌，其流弊亦有不可胜言者！”
en: “The plan is well framed,” Wang replied. “With that provision, the gentry needn't fear official interference and can act freely. But everything depends first on finding the right people. There are plenty of disreputable gentry too. If they choose to appropriate the money and monopolise control, any official who asks questions can be fended off with the imperial edict. The abuses could be endless.”

zh: 俞师爷点点头说：“浙江不知会派谁？想来戴醇士总有份的。”
en: Yu nodded. “I wonder who will be appointed in Zhejiang. Dai Chunshi will surely be among them.”

zh: “戴醇士是谁？”王有龄问，“是不是那位画山水出名的戴侍郎？”
en: “Who is Dai Chunshi?” Wang asked. “Is he the former vice-minister famous for his landscape paintings?”

zh: “对了！正是他。”
en: “Yes, exactly.”

zh: 过了几天，果然邸报载着上谕：“命在籍前任兵部侍郎戴熙，内阁学士朱品芳、朱兰，湖南巡抚陆费瑔等督办浙江团练事宜。”陆费瑔不姓陆，是姓陆费，只有浙江嘉兴才有这一族。
en: A few days later, the gazette did indeed carry an edict appointing the retired vice-minister of War Dai Xi, grand secretariat academicians Zhu Pinfang and Zhu Lan, and Hunan governor Lufei Quan to supervise Zhejiang's militia arrangements. Lufei Quan's surname was not Lu but the compound Lufei, belonging to a clan found only in Jiaxing, Zhejiang.

zh: “气运在变了！”俞师爷下一次与王有龄见面时，这样感叹，“本朝有大征伐，最初是用亲贵为‘大将军’，以后是用旗籍大员，亦多是祖上的勋绩军功的世家子弟，现在索性用汉人，而且是文人。此是国事的一大变，不知纸上谈兵的效用如何？”
en: “The times are changing,” Yu remarked at their next meeting. “At the beginning of our dynasty, great campaigns were entrusted to imperial relatives as commanders-in-chief. Later they went to senior banner officials, usually sons of hereditary military families. Now they are being given to Han Chinese—and to scholars at that. This is a great change in the affairs of the state. I wonder how effective warfare learned from books will prove.”
