zh: 王有龄想想这话果然不错，办团练的大臣，除了浙江省以外，外省的，据他所知，湖南是礼部恃郎曾国藩，安徽是内阁学士吕贤基，此外各省莫不是两榜进士出身，在籍的一二品文臣主持其事。内阁学士许乃刽甚至奉旨帮办江南军务，书生下但握兵权，而且要上战场了。
en: Wang reflected that it was true. Beyond Zhejiang, the militia organisers he knew of included Vice-Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan in Hunan and Grand Secretariat Academician Lü Xianji in Anhui. Elsewhere too, the work was led by senior civil officials of the first or second rank, living at home, who had risen through the examinations. Grand Secretariat Academician Xu Naizhao had even been ordered to assist with military affairs in the lower Yangtze region. Scholars were not merely commanding troops; they were going to the battlefield.

zh: “雪轩兄！”俞师爷又说，“时逢盛世，固然是修来的福分，时逢乱世，也是有作为的人的良机，象我依人作嫁，游幕终老，可以说此生已矣，你却不可错过这个良机！”
en: “Brother Xuexuan,” Yu continued, “living in a peaceful age is a blessing. But troubled times offer an opportunity to men who can accomplish things. I spend my life preparing the way for others, moving from one private staff to another. My own course is already set. You must not miss this chance.”

zh: 受到这番鼓励的王有龄，雄心壮志，越发跃然，因而用世之心，格外迫切，朝朝盼望麟佳归来，谒见奉委之后，好切切实实来做一番事业。
en: Such encouragement made Wang's ambition burn more brightly and his desire to serve more urgent. Every day he awaited Lingui's return, hoping that after an audience and an appointment he could finally begin some real work.

zh: 这天晚上吃过饭，刚刚摊开一张自己所画的地图，预备在灯下对照着读《圣武记》，忽然高升戴着一顶红缨帽，进门便请安：“恭喜老爷，藩台的委札下来了！”
en: One evening after supper, Wang had just spread out a map he had drawn himself, intending to consult it while reading Records of Imperial Military Achievements by lamplight. Gao suddenly entered in a red-tasselled hat and saluted. “Congratulations, Your Honour! Your appointment from the provincial treasurer has arrived!”

zh: “什么？”这时王有龄才发觉高升手中有一封公文。
en: “What?” Only then did Wang notice the official document in Gao's hand.

zh: “藩台衙门派专人送来的。”说着他把委札递了上去。
en: “The treasury sent it by special messenger.” Gao presented it.

zh: 打开来一看，是委王有龄做“海运局”的“坐办”。这个衙门，专为漕米改为海运而设，“总办”由藩司兼领，“坐办”才是实际的主持人。王有龄未得正印官，不免失望，但总是一桩喜事，便问，“人呢？”
en: Wang opened it. He was appointed executive director of the Sea Transport Bureau. This office had been established specifically to manage the change from canal to sea transport for the grain tax. The provincial treasurer concurrently held the title of director-general, but the executive director was the man actually in charge. Wang was disappointed not to receive a substantive local magistracy, yet it was still good news. “Where is he?” he asked.

zh: 那是指送委札的人，高升答道：“还在外头。是藩台衙门的书办。”
en: He meant the messenger. Gao replied, “Still outside. He's a clerk from the provincial treasury.”

zh: “噢！”他跟高升商量，“你看要不要见他？”
en: “Oh.” Wang consulted him. “Do you think I should receive him?”

zh: “见倒不必了。不过要发赏。”
en: “There is no need, but he should be given a reward.”

zh: “那自然，自然。”
en: “Of course, of course.”

zh: 王太太是早就想到了，有人来送委札必要发赏，一个红纸包已包好了多日，这时便亲自拿了出来。
en: Mrs Wang had thought of that long before. An appointment messenger would expect a reward, and she had kept a red packet ready for days. She now brought it out herself.

zh: 高升急忙又替太太请安道喜，夫妇俩又互相道贺。等把四两银子的红包拿了出去，家里的老妈子、厨子、轿班，得到消息，约齐了来磕头贺喜，王太太又要发赏，每人一两银子。这一夜真是皆大欢喜，只有王有龄微觉美中不足。
en: Gao hurriedly saluted and congratulated her too, and husband and wife exchanged congratulations. After the packet of four taels had been taken outside, the older maids, cook, and chair-bearers heard the news and came together to kneel and offer their good wishes. Mrs Wang rewarded each with a tael. Everyone was happy that night. Only Wang felt that something was still missing.

zh: 乱过一阵，他才想起一件要紧事，把高升找了来问道：“藩台是不是回来了？”
en: After the bustle subsided, he remembered an important question and called Gao back. “Has the provincial treasurer returned?”

zh: “今天下午到了，一到就‘上院’，必是抚台交代得很结实，所以连夜把委札送了来。”
en: “He arrived this afternoon and went straight to see the governor. The instructions must have been emphatic, since your appointment was sent out this very evening.”

zh: “那明于一早要去谢委。”
en: “Then I must go early tomorrow to thank him.”

zh: “是！我已经交代轿班了，谢了委还要拜客，我此刻要在门房里预备。顶要紧一张拜客的名单，漏一个就得罪人。“
en: “Yes. I've already told the bearers. After that, you'll have calls to make. I'm going to the gatehouse now to prepare. Most important is the visiting list. Leave out one name, and you've offended someone.”

zh: 王有龄非常满意，连连点头。等高升退了出去，在门房里开拟名单，预备手本，他也在上房里动笔墨，把回杭州谒见黄抚台和奉委海运局坐办的经过，详详细细写了一封信，告诉在江阴的何桂清。
en: Wang nodded repeatedly, thoroughly satisfied. While Gao went to prepare the list and visiting cards, he took up his own brush in the private rooms. He wrote a detailed letter to He Guiqing at Jiangyin, describing his return to Hangzhou, his audience with Governor Huang, and his appointment as executive director of the Sea Transport Bureau.

zh: 信写完已经十二点，王太太亲自伺候丈夫吃了点心，催他归寝。人在枕上，心却不静，一会儿想到要请个人来办笔墨，一会儿又想到明天谢委，麟藩台会问些什么？再又想到接任的日子，是自己挑，还是听上头吩咐？等把这些事都想停当，已经钟打两下了。
en: By the time he finished, it was midnight. His wife personally brought him a light meal and urged him to bed. His head reached the pillow, but his mind would not rest. First he thought of engaging someone to handle his writing; then of the questions Treasurer Lingui might ask the next day. Would he choose his own date for taking office, or await instructions? By the time he had settled these matters in his mind, the clock was striking two.

zh: 也不过睡了三个钟点，便即起身。人逢喜事精神爽，一点都看不出少睡的样子，到了藩台衙门，递上手本，麟桂立即请见。
en: He rose after only three hours' sleep. Happiness had refreshed him so completely that he showed no sign of the short night. At the provincial treasury, he submitted his card and was admitted at once.

zh: 磕头谢委，寒暄了一阵。麟桂很坦率地说：“你老哥是抚台交下来的人，我将来仰仗的地方甚多，凡事不必客气，反正有抚台在那里，政通人和，有些事你就自己作主好了。”
en: After Wang had knelt in thanks for the appointment and the customary greetings were over, Lingui spoke frankly. “You are the man the governor has sent me. I shall have much to rely on you for. There's no need to stand on ceremony. With the governor behind us, cooperation should be easy. You may decide some matters yourself.”

zh: 王有龄一听这话，醋意甚浓，赶紧欠身答道：“不敢！我虽承抚台看得起，实在出于大人的栽培，尊卑有别，也是朝廷体制所关，凡事自然秉命而行。”
en: Wang detected a strong note of resentment and quickly leaned forward. “I would not presume. Though the governor has favoured me, it is truly to Your Excellency that I owe my advancement. The distinction between superior and subordinate is part of the state's proper order. Naturally, I shall act on your instructions in everything.”

zh: “不是，不是！”麟桂不断摇手，“我不是跟你说什么生分的话，也不是推责任，真正是老实话。这位抚台不容易伺候，漕运的事更难办，我的前任为些把条老命都送掉，所以不瞒你老哥说，兄弟颇有戒心。现在海运一事，千斤重担你一肩挑了过去，再好都没有。将来如何办理，你不妨多探探抚台的口气。我是垂拱而治，过一过手转上去，公事只准不驳，岂不是大家都痛快？”
en: “No, no!” Lingui waved his hands. “I'm not trying to keep you at a distance or shift responsibility. I mean what I say. This governor is difficult to serve, and grain transport is more difficult still. My predecessor lost his life over it, so I admit that I am wary. Nothing could be better than having you take this heavy burden of sea transport on your shoulders. As to how it is managed, you would do well to find out the governor's wishes. I can sit back, pass your submissions on, and approve rather than reject them. Wouldn't that suit everyone?”

zh: 倒真的是老实话！王有龄心想，照这样子看，是黄宗汉要来管海运，委自己出个面。麟桂只求不生麻烦，办得好，“保案”里少不了他的名字，办不好有抚台在上面顶着，也可无事，这个打算是不错的。
en: He was indeed speaking honestly. Wang concluded that Huang intended to control sea transport himself and had appointed Wang to act on his behalf. Lingui merely wished to avoid trouble. If the work went well, his name would appear in the recommendations for rewards; if badly, the governor above him would bear the burden. It was a sensible calculation.

zh: 于是他不多说什么，只很恭敬地答道：“我年轻识浅，一切总要求大人教导。”
en: Wang therefore said little, replying only with respect, “I am young and inexperienced. I shall look to Your Excellency for guidance in everything.”

zh: “教导不敢当。不过海运是从我手里办起来的，一切情形，可以先跟你说一说。”
en: “I can hardly call it guidance. But since the sea-transport arrangements began under me, I can explain the situation to you.”

zh: “是！”他把腰挺一挺，身子凑前些，聚精会神地听着。
en: “Yes, Your Excellency.” Wang straightened, leaned forward, and listened closely.

zh: “我先请问，你老哥预备哪一天接事？”
en: “First, when do you intend to take up your duties?”

zh: “要请大人吩咐。”
en: “I await Your Excellency's instructions.”

zh: “总是越快越好！”麟桂喊道：“来啊！”
en: “The sooner the better.” Lingui called, “Attend me!”

zh: 唤来听差，叫取皇历来翻了翻，第三天就是宜于上任的黄道吉日，决定就在这天接事。
en: He sent an attendant for the imperial almanac and examined it. The day after next was auspicious for assuming office, so that date was chosen.

zh: “再有一件事要请问，你老哥‘夹袋’里有几个人？”
en: “One other question. How many men have you ready to bring with you?”

zh: 王有龄一个“班底”也没有，如果是放了州县缺，还要找俞师爷去找人，海运局的情形不知如何？一时无法作答。就在这踌躇之间，忽然想到了一个人，必须替他留个位置。
en: Wang had no staff of his own. Had he obtained a magistracy, he would have asked Yu to find suitable men. He knew nothing of the Sea Transport Bureau's requirements and could not answer immediately. While hesitating, he suddenly remembered someone for whom he must reserve a position.

zh: “只有一个人，姓胡，人极能干。就不知他肯不肯来？”
en: “Only one man, surnamed Hu. He's extremely capable, though I don't know whether he'll agree to come.”

zh: “既然如此，海运局里的旧人，请老哥尽力维持。”
en: “In that case, please do your best to retain the bureau's existing staff.”

zh: 原来如此！麟藩台是怕他一接事，自己有批人要安插，所以预先招呼。
en: So that was it. Lingui feared that Wang would arrive with a group of his own followers to install and was making his wishes known in advance.

zh: 王有龄觉得这位藩台倒是老实人，“我听大人的吩咐。”他又安了个伏笔，“倘或抚台有人交下来，那时再来回禀大人，商量安置的办法。”
en: Wang thought the treasurer an honest enough man. “I shall follow Your Excellency's instructions.” He also left room for a possibility. “If the governor sends anyone to be placed, I shall report to you and discuss the arrangements.”

zh: “好，好！”麟桂接着便谈到海运，“江浙漕米改为海运，由新近调补的江苏藩司倪良耀总办。这位仁兄，你要当心他！”
en: “Very good.” Lingui turned to the business itself. “The change to sea transport for the grain of Jiangsu and Zhejiang is under the overall supervision of Ni Liangyao, recently appointed provincial treasurer of Jiangsu. You must be careful with him.”

zh: “噢！”这是要紧地方，王有龄特为加了几分注意。
en: “Oh?” Wang paid particular attention. This was important.

zh: “亏得我们抚台圣眷隆，靠山硬，不然真叫他给坑了！”
en: “It's fortunate that our governor enjoys imperial favour and has powerful backing. Otherwise, Ni might really have landed us in trouble.”

zh: 原来倪良耀才具有限，总办江浙海运，不甚顺利，朝廷严旨催促，倪良耀便把责任推到浙江，说浙江的新漕才到了六万余石。其实已有三十几万石运到上海，黄宗汉据实奏复，因而有上谕切责倪良耀。
en: Ni had limited ability, and his management of the two provinces' sea shipments had not gone smoothly. Faced with stern imperial orders to hasten the work, he shifted responsibility onto Zhejiang, claiming that only sixty thousand-odd shi of its new grain had arrived. In fact, more than three hundred thousand shi had already reached Shanghai. Huang reported the facts, and an imperial edict sharply rebuked Ni.

zh: “有这个过节儿在那里，事情便难办了。倪良耀随时会找毛病，你要当心。此其一。”
en: “With that grievance between us, the business will be difficult. Ni will be looking for faults at every opportunity. You must be careful. That's the first point.”

zh: “是。”王有龄问道：“请示其二。”
en: “Yes. What is the second?”

zh: “二呢，我们浙江有些地方也很难弄。尤其是湖州府，地方士绅把持，大户欠粮的极多。今年新漕，奉旨提前启运，限期上越发紧迫。前任知府，误漕撤任，我现在在想……”
en: “Some places in Zhejiang are difficult too, especially Huzhou. The local gentry dominate affairs, and many large landholders owe grain taxes. This year's new grain must be dispatched early by imperial order, so the deadline is tighter than ever. The previous prefect was dismissed for delaying the shipments. I am now considering...”

zh: 麟桂忽然不说下去了。这是什么意思呢？王有龄心里思量：莫非要委署湖州府？这也不对啊！州县班子尚未署过实缺，何能平白开擢？也许是委署湖州府属的哪一县。果真如此，就太妙了！湖州府属七县，漕米最多的乌程。归安、德清三县。此三县富庶有名，一补就先补上一等大县，干个两三年，上头有人照应，升知府就有望了。
en: Lingui suddenly stopped. What did he mean? Wang wondered. Was he thinking of appointing him acting prefect of Huzhou? That could not be right. Wang belonged to the magistrates' category and had never even acted in a substantive post. How could he be promoted out of nowhere? Perhaps he meant one of Huzhou's counties. That would be splendid. Of the prefecture's seven counties, Wucheng, Gui'an, and Deqing produced the most grain tax. All three were famously prosperous. To begin with a first-class county, serve for two or three years, and have someone above him offering support—then a prefecture might be within reach.

zh: “总而言之一句话，外面一个倪良耀，里面一个湖州府，把这两外对付得好，事情就容易了。其余的，等你接了事再说吧！”麟桂说到这里端茶碗送客。
en: “In short, there is Ni Liangyao outside the province and Huzhou within it. Handle those two well, and the rest will be easier. We can discuss other matters once you've taken over.” Lingui lifted his teacup to end the audience.

zh: 出了藩台衙门，随即到抚署谒见。刘二非常亲热地道了喜，接着便说，“上头正邀了‘杭嘉湖’、‘宁绍台’两位道台在谈公事，只怕没有工夫见王大老爷。我先去跑一趟看。”
en: Leaving the treasury, Wang went straight to the governor's office. Liu greeted him with warm congratulations, then said, “His Excellency is discussing business with the intendants of the Hangzhou–Jiaxing–Huzhou and Ningbo–Shaoxing–Taizhou circuits. He may not have time to receive you. I'll go and see.”

zh: 果然，黄宗汉正邀了两个“兵备道”在谈出省堵敌的公事，无暇接见，但叫刘二传下话来：接事以后，好好整顿，不必有所瞻顾。又说，等稍为空一空，会来邀他上院，详谈一切。
en: Huang was indeed consulting the two military circuit intendants about sending troops beyond the province to block the enemy. He had no time for Wang, but sent instructions through Liu: after taking over, Wang was to put the bureau in order without being constrained by other considerations. When a little time became available, Huang would summon him for a full discussion.

zh: 所谓“不必瞻顾”，自是指麟桂而言。把抚、藩两上司的话合在一起来看，王有龄才知道自己名为坐办，实在已挑起了总负浙江漕米海运的全责。
en: The instruction not to be constrained plainly referred to Lingui. Taken together, the words of governor and treasurer showed Wang that, though nominally executive director, he had in fact assumed full responsibility for Zhejiang's grain shipments by sea.

zh: “我跟王大老爷说句私说，”刘二把他拉到一边，悄悄说道，“上头有话风出来了：如今军务吃紧，漕米关系军食，朝廷极其关切。只要海运办得不误限期，这一案中可以特保王某，请朝廷破格擢用。是祸是福，都在王某自己。”
en: “Let me tell you something privately,” Liu said, drawing him aside. “His Excellency has let it be known that, with military affairs so urgent, grain supplies concern the army's food, and the court is watching closely. If the sea shipments meet their deadlines, he can make a special recommendation for your exceptional promotion. Whether it brings you fortune or disaster is in your own hands.”

zh: “真正是，抚台如此看得起我，我不知说什么好了。得便请你回一声，就就我决不负抚台的提拔。”
en: “The governor thinks so highly of me that I scarcely know what to say. When you have a chance, please tell him that I shall not disappoint the confidence he has shown in promoting me.”

zh: 刘二答应一定把话转到。接着悄悄递过来两张履历片陪笑道：“一个是我娘舅，一个是我拜把兄弟，请王大老爷栽培。”
en: Liu promised to convey the message. Then he discreetly handed Wang two biographical cards and smiled ingratiatingly. “One is my mother's brother; the other is my sworn brother. I hope Your Honour can find places for them.”

zh: “好，好！”王有龄一口答应，看也不看，就把条子收了起来。
en: “Certainly, certainly.” Wang agreed at once and put the cards away without reading them.

zh: 由此开始拜客，高升早已预备了一张名单，按照路途近远，顺路而去。
en: He then began making his official calls, following the list Gao had prepared in an order that avoided unnecessary travel.

zh: 驻防将军、臬司、盐运使、杭嘉湖道、杭州府都算是上司，须用手本，仁和、钱塘两县平行用拜帖，此外是候补的道府、州县，仅不过到门拜帖，主人照例挡驾，却跑了一天都跑不完。
en: The garrison general, judicial commissioner, salt commissioner, Hangzhou–Jiaxing–Huzhou circuit intendant, and prefect of Hangzhou all counted as superiors and required formal visiting cards. The magistrates of Renhe and Qiantang were his equals and received ordinary cards. Beyond them were the expectant intendants, prefects, and magistrates. Most calls amounted only to leaving a card at the gate, since the host customarily declined to receive visitors. Even so, a whole day was not enough to finish.

zh: 回到家，特为又派人到臬司衙门把俞师爷请来吃便饭，一在把杯小酌，一面说了这天抚、藩两宪的态度。俞师爷很替他高兴，说这个“坐办”的差使，通常该委候补道，至少也得一名候补知府，以王有龄的身分，派季这个差使，那是逾格的提拔，不该为不得州县正堂而烦恼。
en: Back home, Wang sent specially to invite Yu to dinner. Over a little wine, he described the attitudes of the governor and treasurer. Yu was delighted for him. The executive directorship, he explained, would ordinarily go to an expectant circuit intendant, or at least an expectant prefect. For someone of Wang's standing, it was exceptional advancement. He should not regret failing to obtain a magistracy.

zh: 这一番话说得王有龄余憾尽释，便向他讨教接事的规矩，又“要个办笔墨的朋友”，俞师爷推荐了他的一个姓周的表弟，保证勤快可靠。王有龄欣然接纳，约定第二天就下“关书”。
en: This removed Wang's remaining disappointment. He asked about the procedures for taking office and requested a reliable man to handle his writing. Yu recommended a cousin surnamed Zhou, guaranteeing his diligence and trustworthiness. Wang gladly accepted and agreed to issue the formal letter of engagement the next day.

zh: “还有件事要向老兄请教。”他把刘二的两张履历，拿给俞师爷看：“是抚署刘二的来头，一个是他娘舅，一个是他拜把兄弟。“
en: “There is something else on which I'd like your advice.” He showed Yu the two biographical cards. “These come through Liu Er at the governor's office. One is his uncle; the other his sworn brother.”

zh: “什么娘舅兄弟？”俞师爷笑道，“ 都是在刘二那里花了钱的，说至亲兄弟，托词而已！”
en: “Uncle and brother indeed!” Yu laughed. “They've paid Liu for his help. The family relationships are merely a pretext.”

zh: “原来如此！”王有龄又长了一分见识，“想来年长的是‘娘舅’，年轻的是‘兄弟’。你看看如问安插？”
en: “So that's it!” Wang had learned another lesson. “I suppose the older one is the uncle and the younger one the brother. How should I place them?”

zh: “刘二是头千年老狐狸，不买帐固不可，太买帐也不好，当你老实好欺，得寸进尺，以后有碍麻烦。”
en: “Liu is an old fox of the first order. You cannot ignore him, but you shouldn't oblige him too readily either. If he thinks you easy to deceive, he'll keep asking for more and cause endless trouble.”

zh: 俞师爷代他作主，看两个人都有“未入流”的功名，年轻的精力较好，派了“押运要员”，年长的坐得住，派在收发上帮忙。处置妥帖，王有龄心悦诚服。
en: Yu decided the matter for him. Both men held official qualifications below the recognised ranks. The younger, with more energy, could be made a transport escort officer; the older, better suited to sedentary work, could assist with incoming and outgoing correspondence. The arrangement was so appropriate that Wang accepted it with complete satisfaction.

zh: 接享受贺，热闹了两三天，才得静下心来办事，第一步先看来往文卷。
en: Taking office and receiving congratulations occupied two or three noisy days. Only then could he settle down to work. His first task was to examine the correspondence and case files.

zh: 这时他才知道，黄宗汉奏报，已有三十余万石漕米运到上海交倪良耀之说，有些不尽实，实际上大部分的漕注还在运河粮船上，未曾交出，倘或出了意外，责任不轻，得要赶紧催运。
en: He now discovered that Huang's report that more than three hundred thousand shi had reached Shanghai and been delivered to Ni was not entirely accurate. Most of the grain was still aboard canal boats and had not been handed over. Any mishap would carry serious responsibility. The shipments had to be hurried forward.

zh: 正在踌躇苦思之时，黄宗汉特为派了个“文巡捕”来，说：“有紧要公事，请王大老爷即刻上院。”到了抚台衙门，先叩谢宪恩，黄宗汉坦然坐受，等他起身，随即递了一封公事过来，说道：“你先看一看这道上谕。”
en: While he was pondering the difficulty, Huang sent a civil affairs officer with a message: “There is urgent official business. His Honour Wang is to come at once.” On arrival, Wang first knelt to thank the governor for his favour. Huang received the gesture without protest. As soon as Wang rose, he handed him a document. “Read this imperial edict first.”

zh: 王有龄知道，这是军机处转达的谕旨，称为“延寄”，不过虽久闻其名，却还是第一次瞻仰，只见所谓“煌煌天语”，不过普通的宣纸白单帖所写，每页五行，每行二十字，既无钤印，亦无签押，如果不是那个铃了军机处印的封套，根本就不能相信这张不起眼的纸，便是圣旨。
en: Wang knew that an imperial instruction transmitted through the Grand Council was called a court dispatch. He had often heard of such documents, but this was the first he had seen. The supposedly resplendent words of the sovereign were written on ordinary folded xuan paper, five lines to a page and twenty characters to a line. There was neither a seal nor a signature. Without the envelope bearing the Grand Council's seal, he could scarcely have believed that such an unremarkable sheet was an imperial edict.

zh: 一面这样想，一面双手捧着看完，他的记性好，只看了一遍，就把内容都记住了。
en: Thinking this, he read it through while holding it respectfully in both hands. His memory was good, and one reading fixed the whole content in his mind.

zh: 这道上谕仍旧是在催运漕米，对于倪良耀一再申述所派委员，不甚得力，朝廷颇为不耐，严词切贡，最后指令“该藩司即将浙省运到米石，井苏省起运未完米石，仍遵叠奉谕旨，赶紧催办，务令克期放洋。倘再稍有延误，朕必将倪良耀从重冶罪。”
en: Once again, the edict urged haste in the grain shipments. The court had grown impatient with Ni Liangyao's repeated complaints that his appointed agents were ineffective and rebuked him sharply. It concluded: “The provincial treasurer shall, in accordance with the repeated imperial commands, expedite the grain received from Zhejiang together with that of Jiangsu still awaiting dispatch, ensuring that the vessels put to sea by the prescribed date. Should there be the slightest further delay, I shall punish Ni Liangyao severely.”

zh: “我另外接得京里的信，”黄宗汉说，“从扬州失守以后，守将为防长毛东窜，要放闸泄尽淮水，让贼舟动弹不得。如果到了高邮、宝应，还要决洪泽湖淹长毛，那时汪洋一片，百姓一起淹在里面，本年新漕也就泡汤了。为此之故，对海运的漕米，催得急如星火。倪良耀再办不好，一定摘顶戴，我们浙江也得盘算一下。“
en: “I have also received a letter from the capital,” Huang said. “Since Yangzhou fell, the defending commanders have proposed opening the sluices to drain the Huai waters and prevent the rebels' boats from moving east. If they reach Gaoyou and Baoying, the embankments of Lake Hongze may be breached to drown them. The whole region would become a sea, the people would drown with the enemy, and this year's grain would be lost as well. That's why the demand for sea shipments is now so urgent. If Ni fails again, he'll certainly lose his rank. We in Zhejiang must consider our position too.”

zh: 王有龄极细心地听着，等听到最后一句，随即完全明白，浙江的漕米实在也没有运足，万一倪良耀革职查办，那时无所顾忌，将实情和盘托出，黄抚台奏报不实，这一下出的纰漏可就大了。
en: Wang listened closely. At the last sentence, he understood everything. Zhejiang had not actually delivered its full quota. If Ni were dismissed and investigated, he would have nothing left to lose and might reveal all the facts. Huang's inaccurate report would then expose him to serious trouble.

zh: 为今之计，除却尽快运米到上海，由海船承兑足额以外，别无善策。他把这番意思说了出来，黄宗汉的脸上没有什么表示。
en: There was only one sound course: get the rice to Shanghai as quickly as possible and have the seagoing vessels accept the full quantity. Wang said so, but Huang showed no reaction.

zh: 没有表示就是表示，表示不满！王有龄心想，除非告诉他，五天或者十天，一定运齐，他是不会满意的。但自己实在没有这个把握，只能这样答道：“我连夜派员去催，总之一丝一毫不敢疏忽。”
en: No reaction was itself a reaction: displeasure. Wang thought that nothing short of a guarantee to deliver everything within five or ten days would satisfy him. Yet he could not honestly offer one. He could only reply, “I'll send agents out tonight to press the shipments forward. I shall neglect nothing, however small.”

zh: “也只好这样了。”黄宗汉淡淡地说了这一句，一端茶碗，自己先站起身来，哈一哈腰，往里走去。
en: “That will have to do.” Huang spoke coolly, lifted his teacup, rose before his guest, gave a slight bow, and went inside.

zh: 王有龄大为沮丧。接事数天，第一次见抚台，落得这样一个局面，不但伤心，而且寒心，黄抚台是这样对部属，实在难伺候。
en: Wang was deeply discouraged. Only a few days into the job, his first working audience had ended like this. He felt not merely hurt but chilled. A superior who treated his subordinates in such a manner would indeed be difficult to serve.

zh: 坐在轿子里，闷闷不乐，前两天初坐大轿，左顾右盼的那份得意心情，已消失无余。想着心事自然也不会注意到经过了哪些地方？就在这迷惘恍惚之中，蓦地里兜起一个影子，急忙顿足喊道：“停轿，停轿！”
en: Sitting in his chair, he brooded. The proud pleasure with which he had looked about on his first rides a few days earlier had vanished. Lost in thought, he scarcely noticed where they were passing. Then, through his distracted state, a figure suddenly caught his eye. Stamping his foot, he shouted, “Stop the chair! Stop!”

zh: 健步如飞的轿班不知怎么回事，拼命煞住脚，还是冲了好几步才能停住。
en: The bearers, moving at a brisk pace, had no idea what was wrong. They tried desperately to halt but carried on for several steps before they could stop.

zh: 挟着“护书”跟在轿旁的高升，立即也赶到轿前，只见主人已掀开轿帘，探出头来，睁大了眼回头向来路上望。
en: Gao, walking beside the chair with the document folder under his arm, hurried to the front. His master had already lifted the curtain and thrust out his head, staring wide-eyed back along the street.

zh: 这个突如其来的动作，引起了路人的好奇，纷纷住足，遥遥注视，高升看看有失体统，便轻喊一声：“老爷！”
en: The sudden commotion drew curious passers-by to a halt. Seeing them watching from a distance, Gao felt that his master's dignity was at risk and called softly, “Your Honour!”

zh: 一见高升，王有龄便说：“快，快，有个穿墨布夹袍的，快拉住他。”
en: At the sight of him, Wang said, “Quick! The man in the black lined robe—stop him!”

zh: 穿黑布夹袍的也多得很，是怎等样一个人呢？高或矮，胖还是瘦，年纪多大，总要略略说明了，才好去找。
en: There were plenty of men in black lined robes. What sort of man did he mean? Tall or short, stout or thin, and how old? Gao needed at least some description before he could search.

zh: 他还在踌躇，王有龄已忍不得了，拼命拍轿杠，要轿班把它成倒，意思是要跨出轿来自己去追。这越发不象样了，高升连声喊道：“老爷，老爷，体统要紧，到底是谁？说了我去找。”
en: While he hesitated, Wang lost patience. He beat on the carrying pole, demanding that the bearers lower the chair so he could leap out and pursue the man himself. This was still less seemly. Gao cried repeatedly, “Your Honour, your dignity! Who is it? Tell me, and I'll find him.”

zh: 还有谁？胡少爷！“
en: “Who else? Young Master Hu!”

zh: “啊！”高升拔脚便奔，“胡少爷”是怎么个人，他听主人说过不止一遍，脑中早有了极深的印象。
en: “Ah!” Gao set off at a run. He had heard his master describe Young Master Hu many times and already had a vivid picture of him in his mind.

zh: 一路追，一路细察行人，倒有个穿黑布袍的，却是花白胡须的老者，再有一个已近中年，形容猥琐，看去不象，姑且请问“尊姓”，却非姓胡。这时高升有些着急，也不免困惑，他相信他主人与胡雪岩虽失之交臂，却决不会看错，然则就此片刻的工夫，会走到哪里去了呢？
en: He ran along, examining the passers-by. One man wore a black robe but had a grey beard. Another was approaching middle age and had an unprepossessing appearance. He did not seem right either, but Gao asked his surname just in case. It was not Hu. Gao grew anxious and puzzled. He trusted that, though his master had only caught a passing glimpse, he could not have mistaken Hu Xueyan. Where could the man have gone in these few moments?
